method: 6 scanners + 1 adversarial verifier per area (atl-accuracy-audit workflow)

confirmed.title: Paint shaders are stored in Java only and never drawn, so <shape><gradient> renders solid black
confirmed.android_behavior: Skia fills with the shader (Linear/Radial/Sweep/BitmapShader) and ignores the paint colour. GradientDrawable relies on this: it sets the paint to opaque black and expects the LinearGradient shader to replace it.
confirmed.impact: Every <shape> with a <gradient> (scrims, header fades, button gradients, splash backgrounds) draws as a solid black box. Custom views that use LinearGradient or RadialGradient draw in the plain paint colour. android_atl_GskCanvas.c has no shader code at all.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Give Shader subclasses real state (points, colours, positions, tile mode, local matrix) and pass it to the native paint. In GskCanvas draw calls use gtk_snapshot_push_linear_gradient / push_radial_gradient / push_conic_gradient (or repeating variants), clipped to the geometry, when paint->shader is set. BitmapShader can map to a texture node.
confirmed.verify_reason: Confirmed: Paint.setShader only stores the shader in a Java field, LinearGradient's constructors have empty bodies, and android_atl_GskCanvas.c has no shader code. GradientDrawable sets mFillPaint to Color.BLACK when there is no solid colour, so gradient shapes fill black.

confirmed.title: native drawRect ignores Paint.Style.STROKE and always fills
confirmed.android_behavior: With STROKE style drawRect outlines the rectangle at the stroke width, and with FILL_AND_STROKE it does both. drawRoundRect and drawPath in the same file already check is_stroke and is_fill.
confirmed.impact: A <shape> with <solid> plus <stroke> and no <corners> (bordered boxes, outlined buttons, input fields, dividers) is painted solid in the stroke colour, hiding the fill and any content drawn under it. Custom views that draw outlined rectangles get filled blocks.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Branch on paint->is_fill and paint->is_stroke as native_drawRoundRect does: append the colour only when is_fill, and for is_stroke build a GskPath rect and gtk_snapshot_append_stroke with paint->gsk_stroke (or use append_border with the half-width offset).
confirmed.verify_reason: Confirmed: native_drawRect always calls gtk_snapshot_append_color with no is_stroke/is_fill branch, while drawPath does branch on them. GskCanvas.drawRect passes straight through to it, and GradientDrawable lines 542-545 call drawRect with a STROKE paint.

confirmed.title: createFromXmlInner returns null or an empty drawable for many standard XML tags
confirmed.android_behavior: DrawableInflater handles selector, animated-selector, level-list, layer-list, transition, ripple, adaptive-icon, color, shape, vector, animated-vector, scale, clip, rotate, animated-rotate, animation-list, inset, bitmap and nine-patch, each inflated from its XML.
confirmed.impact: No error is shown. LayerDrawable.inflate drops null layers, so ProgressBar progress layers built from <clip> vanish. <animated-selector> (AppCompat and Material checkbox, radio and switch drawables) returns null. <rotate> spinners, <level-list> (battery and wifi icons) and <color> items are missing. Transition, animation-list, nine-patch and animated-vector come back blank because their children and attributes are never parsed (the AVD shows nothing instead of its static vector).
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add cases for every tag. Restore ClipDrawable.inflate (currently commented out), implement Scale/Rotate as DrawableWrapper subclasses, inflate level-list, color, nine-patch (android:src) and transition (as a LayerDrawable). Treat animated-selector as a StateListDrawable and animated-vector as its static <vector> target until animation exists. Throw XmlPullParserException for unknown tags as AOSP does, instead of returning null.
confirmed.verify_reason: Confirmed: the createFromXmlInner switch returns new Drawable() for transition and empty NinePatch, AnimationDrawable and AnimatedVectorDrawable objects, and returns null for clip, level-list, rotate, scale, color and animated-selector. No other inflation path handles these tags.

confirmed.title: LayerDrawable.isStateful/onStateChange are commented out, so selectors inside layer-list and ripple never react to state
confirmed.android_behavior: LayerDrawable (and RippleDrawable, which extends it here) is stateful when any layer is stateful, and passes setState on to every layer.
confirmed.impact: Base Drawable.isStateful() returns false, so View never calls setState on a layer-list or ripple background. A <selector> inside a <ripple> or <layer-list> (very common for pressed, checked, selected and disabled backgrounds, including AppCompat and Material button backgrounds) stays in its initial state. Buttons look identical when disabled or pressed, and checked/selected list items don't highlight.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Uncomment isStateful() and onStateChange(), and the LayerState.isStateful() helper (the mHaveStateful cache needs resetting when layers are added). Keep the existing call in inflate().
confirmed.verify_reason: Confirmed: LayerDrawable isStateful and onStateChange (around lines 479-500) are inside block comments. RippleDrawable has no isStateful override, so the base Drawable.isStateful applies and View never calls setState on these backgrounds.

confirmed.title: InsetDrawable ignores insets from both the constructors and XML
confirmed.android_behavior: InsetDrawable shrinks the child's bounds by the insets in onBoundsChange, adds the insets to getIntrinsicWidth/Height and getPadding, and reads android:inset, insetLeft, insetTop, insetRight and insetBottom (dimension or fraction) from XML.
confirmed.impact: <inset> backgrounds draw edge to edge: AppCompat and Material button shapes (abc_btn_default_mtrl_shape, MaterialButton insets), dialog backgrounds with 16dp/24dp insets, and list dividers with left insets. Buttons look larger and touch each other, and dialogs lose their margins.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Store the insets in InsetState. Read R.styleable.InsetDrawable_inset* in an inflate override. Override onBoundsChange to set the child bounds minus the insets, add the insets to getIntrinsicWidth/Height and getPadding, and implement InsetState.newDrawable instead of throwing UnsupportedOperationException.
confirmed.verify_reason: Confirmed: both InsetDrawable constructors drop the insets, there are no inset fields and no inflate override, getPadding returns false, and InsetState.newDrawable throws UnsupportedOperationException.

confirmed.title: BitmapDrawable ignores alpha, tint and colour filter, getPaint() returns a throwaway Paint, and <bitmap> attributes are dropped
confirmed.android_behavior: BitmapDrawable keeps a persistent Paint that setAlpha, setColorFilter and the tint filter all affect. It honours android:tint, gravity (e.g. a centred logo on a splash windowBackground) and tileMode (repeat/mirror patterns).
confirmed.impact: Tinted PNG icons (DrawableCompat.setTint, app:tint, android:tint on <bitmap>, toolbar and menu icons, colorControlNormal tinting) show their original colours. drawable.setAlpha() fades do nothing, and getPaint().setAlpha()/setAntiAlias() are lost. Splash screens using <bitmap android:gravity="center"> stretch the logo across the window, and tiled backgrounds stretch.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep one Paint field and return it from getPaint. Implement setAlpha, getAlpha, setColorFilter, setTintList and setTintMode (and onStateChange for stateful tints), and draw through the GskCanvas with that paint (an opacity node plus a colour-matrix node). Read tint, tintMode, gravity, tileMode and alpha in inflate, and apply gravity and tiling in draw.
confirmed.verify_reason: Confirmed: getPaint returns new Paint(), setGravity and setTileModeX are empty, and there are no setAlpha, setColorFilter or setTintList overrides (the Drawable base versions are empty). inflate only reads BitmapDrawable_src. ImageView does push a colour filter into the drawable, but BitmapDrawable drops it.

confirmed.title: View.setRotation/RotationX/Y, setScaleX/Y and setPivotX/Y are empty and the getters return fixed identity values
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP stores these in the RenderNode and applies them when drawing. Apps use them constantly through View.ROTATION/SCALE_X/SCALE_Y properties, ViewPropertyAnimator.rotation()/scaleX(), ObjectAnimator.ofFloat(v, "rotation", ...) and android:rotation/scaleX in XML.
confirmed.impact: Expand/collapse chevrons never rotate, scale-in/out effects (FAB show/hide, press-bounce, pop-in dialogs) do nothing, and mirrored icons (scaleX=-1) are not flipped. rotationBy() always starts from 0 because getRotation() returns 0. Affects most Material/AndroidX apps.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Store rotation, rotationX/Y, scaleX/Y and pivotX/Y in fields and apply them at snapshot time (gsk transform around the pivot, next to where translation is already applied). Make the getters return the stored state, defaulting the pivot to the view centre as AOSP does. Read android:rotation/scaleX/scaleY/transformPivotX/Y in the constructor.
confirmed.verify_reason: View.java 2534-2550: the setters for rotation, scale and pivot are empty and the getters return constants. Translation is stored (lines 944, 2123) but these are not. No subclass overrides them; the only other setRotation/setScaleX are in VectorDrawable internals. The SCALE_X and ROTATION Properties call these no-ops, and rotationBy uses getRotation(), which is always 0.

confirmed.title: addOnAttachStateChangeListener keeps only one listener, so each call replaces the previous one
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP keeps a CopyOnWriteArrayList of listeners and notifies all of them. AndroidX relies on this: Fragment/ViewTreeLifecycleOwner, Compose's AndroidComposeView and DisposeOnDetachedFromWindow, RecyclerView, Glide's ViewTarget, coroutines' view scopes and Snackbar each register their own listener on the same view.
confirmed.impact: When a second library registers a listener, the first one never fires. Compose content may not dispose or recompose correctly, image loads are not cleared, and lifecycle-scoped jobs leak or never start. These failures are silent and depend on registration order.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use a CopyOnWriteArrayList<OnAttachStateChangeListener> (as for on_layout_change_listeners) and iterate it in onAttachedToWindow/onDetachedFromWindow. Also dispatch from dispatchAttachedToWindow so that subclasses overriding onAttachedToWindow without calling super still notify listeners.
confirmed.verify_reason: Line 1726 assigns a single field and line 2478 declares it. onAttachedToWindow/onDetachedFromWindow (2411, 2424) notify only that one listener. Nothing else in the tree keeps a list, so a second registration silently replaces the first.

confirmed.title: setPaddingRelative() is empty, so padding set from code with start/end is dropped
confirmed.evidence: public void setPaddingRelative(int start, int top, int end, int bottom) {}
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP sets start/top/end/bottom padding, resolved to left/right in LTR. ViewCompat.setPaddingRelative() calls it directly on API 17+. AppCompat, Material components (Chip, MaterialButton, TextInputLayout, Toolbar), RecyclerView item decorations and many apps call it.
confirmed.impact: Views padded from code have no padding: text touches edges, icons overlap labels and list items are cramped. getPaddingStart() still returns the old value, so later measurement math is also wrong.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Implement it as setPadding(start, top, end, bottom) for LTR, or swap start and end when getLayoutDirection() is RTL.
confirmed.verify_reason: Line 2307 is an empty body, and no widget subclass overrides setPaddingRelative.

confirmed.title: canScrollVertically/canScrollHorizontally always return false instead of using computeVertical/HorizontalScroll*
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP View.canScrollVertically(direction) computes offset/range/extent from computeVerticalScrollOffset/Range/Extent. RecyclerView, NestedScrollView and ScrollView do not override canScrollVertically; they override the compute* methods and rely on the base implementation. The base computeVerticalScrollOffset returns mScrollY, not -1.
confirmed.impact: SwipeRefreshLayout.canChildScrollUp() always reports 'at top', so pulling down in a scrolled list starts a refresh instead of scrolling up. CoordinatorLayout/AppBarLayout, ViewPager nested-scroll arbitration and 'scroll to top' FAB visibility logic also misbehave. Affects most list-based apps.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Port the AOSP implementation: offset = computeVerticalScrollOffset(); range = computeVerticalScrollRange() - computeVerticalScrollExtent(); if (range == 0) return false; return direction < 0 ? offset > 0 : offset < range - 1. Do the same horizontally, and make computeVerticalScrollOffset() return scrollY (computeHorizontalScrollOffset() should return scrollX).
confirmed.verify_reason: canScrollVertically (2387) and canScrollHorizontally (2495) return false, and computeVerticalScrollOffset returns -1. AbsListView/GridView override the compute* methods, but the base canScroll* never consults them. AndroidX RecyclerView does not override canScrollVertically, so SwipeRefreshLayout.canChildScrollUp is always false.

confirmed.title: Inflater passes the inflater's root context to factories and children, so android:theme overlays do not cascade
confirmed.android_behavior: In AOSP, rInflate uses parent.getContext() for each child, and createViewFromTag wraps that context in a ContextThemeWrapper for android:theme before calling the factories. AppCompatViewInflater skips reading android:theme on API 21+ because the framework has already done it.
confirmed.impact: ThemeOverlay on a Toolbar, AppBarLayout or card (e.g. android:theme="@style/ThemeOverlay.AppCompat.Dark.ActionBar") does not reach its child views. In AppCompat apps it is ignored even on the view itself, because AppCompat's factory creates the view first with the unwrapped context. Result: dark text and icons on dark toolbars, wrong accent colours. Affects most AppCompat/Material apps.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Thread a Context through createViewFromTag/rInflate like AOSP: use parent.getContext() for children, apply the android:theme wrapper in createViewFromTag before trying the factories, and pass the wrapped context to createView instead of this.context.
confirmed.verify_reason: createViewFromTag passes this.context to the factories (line 152). createView uses this.context and wraps android:theme only for that one view (106-111). rInflate never uses parent.getContext(), so the overlay does not reach the children. AppCompat skips android:theme on API 21+, so on the factory path the overlay is ignored even on the view itself.

confirmed.title: TextView.setCompoundDrawablesWithIntrinsicBounds / ...Relative... are empty, XML drawableStart/Left/Top are never read, and getCompoundDrawables returns an empty array
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP sets each drawable's bounds to its intrinsic size and calls setCompoundDrawables. It also reads android:drawableLeft/Start/Top/Right/End/Bottom in the constructor, and getCompoundDrawables returns the drawables currently set. These are the main ways apps put icons next to text in labels, menu rows and settings rows. A grep for TextView_drawable in api-impl finds no reader.
confirmed.impact: Icons next to text never show, whether set from XML or from code with the WithIntrinsicBounds variants, which nearly every app uses. Code that reads getCompoundDrawables()[i] to tint or animate an icon gets null and either crashes or does nothing.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Implement the WithIntrinsicBounds variants as AOSP does (setBounds(0,0,getIntrinsicWidth,getIntrinsicHeight), then setCompoundDrawables). Read the TextView_drawable* attributes in the constructor. Return the stored drawableLeft/Top/Right/Bottom from getCompoundDrawables and getCompoundDrawablesRelative.
confirmed.verify_reason: TextView.java lines 417-433 have the empty WithIntrinsicBounds overloads, and getCompoundDrawables/Relative return new Drawable[4] even though the drawableLeft etc. fields are stored. Nothing in api-impl reads TextView_drawable*. Only setCompoundDrawables(Relative) works.

confirmed.title: CompoundButton/CheckBox/RadioButton.setOnClickListener is a no-op
confirmed.android_behavior: In AOSP, CompoundButton.performClick toggles the checked state and then calls the View's OnClickListener. Many apps attach the click listener to a CheckBox or RadioButton and read isChecked() inside it.
confirmed.impact: Tapping a checkbox or radio button whose app logic hangs off setOnClickListener visibly toggles it, but nothing happens: settings are not saved and dependent UI does not update. This is common in to-do apps, settings screens and dialogs.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Store the listener and call it from the native toggled/state-set handler (or route the GTK click through View.performClick) after the state changes.
confirmed.verify_reason: CompoundButton, CheckBox and RadioButton all override setOnClickListener with an empty body. The native side hooks only toggled/state-set for OnCheckedChangeListener, so an OnClickListener set on a checkbox never fires.

confirmed.title: EditText.getText()/getEditableText() return a detached copy, so editing the Editable has no effect
confirmed.android_behavior: getText() returns the live Editable buffer, so editText.getText().clear(), .append(), .insert() and .replace() change the field. The Editable passed to TextWatcher.afterTextChanged is the same live buffer, and formatters (phone numbers, masks) edit it in place.
confirmed.impact: The common 'clear the input after sending' pattern (getText().clear()) leaves the text in the field. Input masks and auto-formatting in afterTextChanged are silently dropped. This affects chat, search, calculator and form apps.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Return an Editable subclass that writes changes back to the GtkText buffer, or keep a Java-side Editable in sync with the native buffer and push modifications back to it.
confirmed.verify_reason: EditText.getText and getEditableText return new SpannableStringBuilder(native_getText(widget)), a detached copy. Calling clear(), append() and the like on it does not change the GtkText.

confirmed.title: onEditorAction is called with actionId 0 and a KeyEvent whose action is 3 (IME_ACTION_SEARCH passed as KeyEvent action)
confirmed.evidence:
jobject key_event = J_new__KeyEvent(env, (jlong)0, (jlong)0, IME_ACTION_SEARCH, KEYCODE_ENTER, 0, 0);
J__TextView__OnEditorActionListener__onEditorAction(env, d->listener, d->this, 0, key_event);
confirmed.android_behavior: On Enter, Android calls onEditorAction(v, actionId=<the configured imeOptions action, e.g. IME_ACTION_SEARCH/DONE/SEND>, event). For a hardware Enter it passes actionId IME_NULL with a KeyEvent where getAction()==ACTION_DOWN(0). Apps check `actionId == EditorInfo.IME_ACTION_SEARCH || (event != null && event.getAction() == KeyEvent.ACTION_DOWN && event.getKeyCode() == KEYCODE_ENTER)`. The ATL KeyEvent(long,long,int action,int code,int repeat,int meta) constructor stores the third argument as mAction.
confirmed.impact: Pressing Enter in search fields and message boxes fails both common checks (actionId is 0 and event.getAction() is 3), so searches are not submitted and messages are not sent from the keyboard.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pass KeyEvent.ACTION_DOWN as the KeyEvent action and pass the view's imeOptions action (store it in setImeOptions, which is currently empty) as actionId.
confirmed.verify_reason: on_activate builds J_new__KeyEvent(0,0,IME_ACTION_SEARCH(3),KEYCODE_ENTER,0,0), and the KeyEvent ctor stores the third argument as mAction. actionId is passed as 0, and setImeOptions is empty. Checks for actionId==IME_ACTION_* or getAction()==ACTION_DOWN fail. Checks that only test the keycode still pass.

confirmed.title: ImageView.setColorFilter(...) overloads are all empty
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP applies the color filter to the image drawable. This is the standard way to tint icons at runtime, for example imageView.setColorFilter(ContextCompat.getColor(..)) to switch an icon to the theme or accent colour or show a selected state.
confirmed.impact: Icons tinted at runtime keep their original colour: often black-on-dark or white-on-white icons, and no selected or unselected feedback. Very many apps tint toolbar or list icons this way.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Store the filter in colorFilter and reapply it to the current drawable (mutate + setColorFilter), the same way setImageTintList already does.
confirmed.verify_reason: All three setColorFilter overloads in ImageView.java are empty, including the final one. Only the XML tint and setImageTintList apply a filter.

confirmed.title: setImageBitmap and setImageResource (bitmap path) never update the drawable field, so getDrawable() is stale or null and the tint is lost
confirmed.android_behavior: Both methods wrap the image in a BitmapDrawable and go through updateDrawable, so getDrawable() returns it, the ImageView's tint and colour filter apply, and the old drawable's callback is cleared.
confirmed.impact: ((BitmapDrawable)iv.getDrawable()).getBitmap() returns null or the previous image, which causes crashes or wrong shares and saves in gallery or avatar code. android:tint is ignored for every PNG set with setImageResource. The previous drawable keeps its callback to this view.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Route both through setImageDrawable(new BitmapDrawable(getResources(), bitmap)) (or getContext().getDrawable(resid)) so the drawable state stays consistent.
confirmed.verify_reason: setImageBitmap and the bitmap path of setImageResource call native_setDrawable directly and never assign this.drawable, so getDrawable() returns the stale drawable. The colorFilter is not applied and the old drawable keeps its callback.

confirmed.title: maxLines/singleLine/lines/ellipsize are ignored from XML and code; the label always wraps freely
confirmed.android_behavior: android:maxLines="1" with ellipsize="end" (or singleLine) truncates with an ellipsis. This is almost universal for titles and subtitles in list rows.
confirmed.impact: List rows, toolbar titles and cards grow to several lines instead of truncating, which pushes layouts out of shape. Fixed-height rows overflow or get clipped mid-line.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Read maxLines, lines, singleLine and ellipsize in the constructor. Map them to gtk_label_set_lines plus gtk_label_set_ellipsize (and wrap=FALSE for singleLine), and store the values for the getters.
confirmed.verify_reason: setSingleLine, setEllipsize, setMaxLines and setLines are empty, and getMaxLines returns -1. The native label is created with wrap=TRUE, and the TextView native code never calls ellipsize or set_lines.

confirmed.title: ProgressBar/SeekBar ignore android:max and android:progress from XML
confirmed.android_behavior: android:max and android:progress set the range and initial value. Seekbars for volume (max=15), seconds (max=60) and so on rely on this.
confirmed.impact: A SeekBar declared with max="10" still ranges 0..100, so the values reported to the app are 10x too large. A ProgressBar with max=1000 clamps setProgress(500) to 100 (full bar). Initial progress from XML is not shown.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Read ProgressBar_max, ProgressBar_min and ProgressBar_progress in the constructor and call setMax and setProgress (SeekBar's overrides then update the GtkRange).
confirmed.verify_reason: The ProgressBar constructor reads only indeterminateDrawable, progressDrawable and indeterminate. A grep finds no reader of ProgressBar_max or ProgressBar_progress. The SeekBar native range is hardcoded to 0..100.

confirmed.title: SharedPreferences change listeners never fire (notifyListeners body commented out)
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP calls onSharedPreferenceChanged on the main thread for every modified key after commit()/apply(). Preference screens and apps register listeners to react to setting changes such as theme, sync interval or notification toggles.
confirmed.impact: registerOnSharedPreferenceChangeListener registers the listener but it is never called. Settings changes have no effect until restart, and screens that update summaries or UI from the listener stay stale. Hits nearly every app with a settings screen.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Uncomment the AOSP body. Call the listeners directly when Looper.myLooper()==Looper.getMainLooper(), otherwise post to new Handler(Looper.getMainLooper()) instead of ActivityThread.sMainThreadHandler.
confirmed.verify_reason: SharedPreferencesImpl.java:464: the whole notifyListeners body is inside a block comment. commit() (line 460) and apply() (line 384) both call it, and register/unregister really do fill mListeners (lines 181 and 187), so registered listeners are never called.

confirmed.title: AlertDialog.Builder.setView(View) drops the custom view
confirmed.android_behavior: Builder.setView sets the dialog's custom content view, used for text-input, number-picker and custom-form dialogs.
confirmed.impact: Framework AlertDialog dialogs built with a custom view (rename/input/password prompts) show only title and buttons, with no input field. The positive-button handler then reads an EditText that was never shown.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Store the view and call dialog.setView(view) (which already maps to setContentView), or forward it directly.
confirmed.verify_reason: Builder.setView(View) (AlertDialog.java around line 129) just returns this and never calls dialog.setView, even though AlertDialog.setView(View) exists and maps to setContentView. Custom-view builder dialogs lose their content.

confirmed.title: AlertDialog button with null listener throws NullPointerException on click
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP lets the listener be null: setNegativeButton("Cancel", null) is the standard idiom, and clicking just dismisses the dialog.
confirmed.impact: Clicking any button registered with a null listener (very common Cancel/OK buttons) crashes the app with an NPE instead of closing the dialog.
confirmed.suggested_fix: if (listener != null) listener.onClick(AlertDialog.this, whichButton); dismiss();
confirmed.verify_reason: AlertDialog.setButton wraps the listener in an OnClickListener that calls listener.onClick(...) without a null check. Builder.setNegativeButton(text, null) passes null straight through, so clicking that button throws an NPE before dismiss() runs.

confirmed.title: Theme.applyStyle/setTo never update ThemeKey, so every Theme shares one drawable/ColorStateList cache bucket
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP Theme.applyStyle calls mKey.append(resId, force) and setTo copies mKey. ThemedResourceCache (used by loadDrawable via mDrawableCacheInternal.put(key, theme, cs) and by the ComplexColor cache) partitions cached entries by that key, so a drawable or ColorStateList resolved against one theme is not reused for another.
confirmed.impact: All non-null themes have an empty, equal ThemeKey. A drawable or color selector whose ?attr values were resolved under one theme (e.g. the activity theme) is handed to views under a different theme (ThemeOverlay toolbar, dialog theme, a second activity with another theme). This gives wrong icon tints, ripple and selector colors and dark/light mismatches in Material/AppCompat apps that use overlays.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In Theme.applyStyle add mKey.append(resid, force). In Theme.setTo add mKey.setTo(other.getKey()) (and recompute the hash code in ThemeKey.setTo as AOSP does). Implement rebase() from the key if needed.
confirmed.verify_reason: Theme.applyStyle (Resources.java:1255) only calls mAssets.applyThemeStyle, and setTo only calls copyTheme. Neither touches mKey (line 1505). getThemedLocked in ThemedResourceCache keys entries by t.getKey(), so every theme shares the empty key (hash 0, equal). loadDrawable reads and writes mDrawableCacheInternal and mColorDrawableCache with the theme, so a drawable resolved under one theme is handed to another.

confirmed.title: requestPermissions never delivers onRequestPermissionsResult; checkPermission denies all unlisted (incl. normal) permissions
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP always answers with onRequestPermissionsResult(requestCode, perms, grantResults), which AndroidX ActivityResult permission launchers depend on. Normal (install-time) permissions declared in the manifest, such as INTERNET, WAKE_LOCK, VIBRATE, FOREGROUND_SERVICE and RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED, are reported GRANTED.
confirmed.impact: Apps that check a permission (e.g. POST_NOTIFICATIONS, CAMERA, or any normal permission) see DENIED and call requestPermissions. The callback never comes, so features wait forever or stay disabled (notification setup, camera/QR scanning, file import) with no error.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In requestPermissions, post to the main looper a call to onRequestPermissionsResult(requestCode, permissions, results), where results come from checkSelfPermission per entry. In PackageManager.checkPermission, return GRANTED for permissions declared in the app manifest with protectionLevel normal.
confirmed.verify_reason: Activity.requestPermissions (line 724) only logs. PackageManager.checkPermission returns DENIED by default for everything except a handful of storage, network and C2DM permissions, which Context.checkSelfPermission reaches through checkCallingOrSelfPermission. Apps asking for permissions outside that list never get onRequestPermissionsResult.

confirmed.title: Intent.resolveActivity returns null for implicit intents ATL can actually handle (VIEW URL, SEND)
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP resolves the intent through PackageManager.resolveActivity and returns the handler's ComponentName. The documented pattern is `if (intent.resolveActivity(pm) != null) startActivity(intent); else showNoAppToast()`.
confirmed.impact: For implicit intents such as ACTION_VIEW with an http(s) URL, ACTION_SEND or mailto, the method returns null even though ContextImpl.startActivity would open them through portals. Apps show "No browser/app found" or silently do nothing for Open link, Share and Email. ATL's own PackageManager.queryIntentActivities special-cases http VIEW, so the two disagree.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Call pm.resolveActivity(this, MATCH_DEFAULT_ONLY) and return its ComponentName. Make PackageManager.resolveActivity return a synthetic ResolveInfo for the intents startActivity handles externally (VIEW with data, SEND, CHOOSER), as queryIntentActivities already does for http.
confirmed.verify_reason: Intent.resolveActivity (line 890) returns the component field, which is null for implicit intents. Meanwhile ContextImpl.startActivity does handle SEND and any intent with data (nativeOpenURI or file open), and PackageManager.queryIntentActivities special-cases http VIEW. The 'resolveActivity != null' guard therefore wrongly blocks working actions.

confirmed.title: PropertyValuesHolder ignores the evaluator for int/float values and ignores keyframes, so ofArgb/ArgbEvaluator color animations interpolate raw ints
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP stores values in a KeyframeSet and always runs them through the TypeEvaluator when one is set (ValueAnimator.ofInt(...).setEvaluator(new ArgbEvaluator()) is the standard color-animation idiom). Keyframes from ofKeyframe() are animated. Fractions outside [0,1] from Overshoot/Anticipate interpolators extrapolate past the end values. clone() copies the evaluator.
confirmed.impact: Any color animation that uses setEvaluator(new ArgbEvaluator()) on int values (toolbar or status-bar color fades, button highlight, Material components) interpolates the packed ARGB int linearly and flashes through unrelated colors. ofKeyframe() animators log 'No values set' and leave the value as a Keyframe object. Overshoot and bounce interpolators are clamped and lose the overshoot. clone() drops the evaluator, so cloned color animators break even with an evaluator.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In calculateValue, when evaluator != null, use it for the int, float and object paths (boxing values). Implement keyframe evaluation: find the surrounding keyframes and apply per-keyframe interpolators. Remove the [0,1] clamp and extrapolate using the first and last segments as AOSP does. Copy the evaluator in clone().
confirmed.verify_reason: calculateValue clamps the fraction to [0,1]. confirmed.title: TextPaint(Paint), TextPaint(int flags) and TextPaint.set() drop the source paint even though Paint(Paint)/set(Paint) exist

/

confirmed.title: Password fields show plaintext: setInputType and setTransformationMethod are empty and no masking exists anywhere

confirmed.title: MediaPlayer stop/pause/release/seekTo/setLooping/setVolume are empty, isPlaying is always false, create(ctx,resId) has no data source

Make prepareAsync fire OnPreparedListener on 'notify::prepared', and wire up the OnError, OnPrepared and OnSeekComplete listeners.

confirmed.title: NetworkCapabilities never includes NET_CAPABILITY_VALIDATED, and NetworkInfo.isAvailable() is always false, so connected networks look unusable
confirmed.android_behavior: A working default network has INTERNET and VALIDATED (plus NOT_SUSPENDED, NOT_ROAMING, NOT_CONGESTED, NOT_VCN_MANAGED). NetworkInfo.isAvailable() is true for a connected network and getTypeName() returns "WIFI" for TYPE_WIFI.

Old 'Wi-Fi only' checks comparing getTypeName() to "WIFI" fail.

NetworkInfo.isAvailable() should return state == CONNECTED, and getTypeName() should return "WIFI" when connected.

confirmed.title: registerDefaultNetworkCallback is a no-op; registerNetworkCallback passes a null Network, never fires an initial onAvailable, and unregister never disconnects

confirmed.impact: Apps that wait for onAvailable before loading content (and libraries like WorkManager's NetworkStateTracker on API 24+, Coil and ExoPlayer requirements) never see a network. Those using registerNetworkCallback get onAvailable(null) only after a change, and their getNetworkCapabilities(network) call then returns null, which they read as offline. Callbacks keep firing into destroyed fragments after unregister.

Implement registerDefaultNetworkCallback the same way. Store the g_signal handler id per callback and g_signal_handler_disconnect it in unregisterNetworkCallback. Only fire on actual availability transitions.

confirmed.title: WebViewClient callbacks use non-AOSP signatures: onPageStarted(WebView,String) and only the String shouldOverrideUrlLoading are called, so app overrides never run

Apps override the 3-arg onPageStarted and the WebResourceRequest variant.

Add shouldOverrideUrlLoading(WebView, WebResourceRequest) whose default delegates to the String version, and have native call the WebResourceRequest variant with a simple WebResourceRequest implementation. Add onReceivedError/shouldInterceptRequest stubs with AOSP signatures.

confirmed.title: Canvas.drawLines steps by 1 float instead of 4, ignores offset+count and reads past the array
confirmed.evidence:
for (int i = offset; i < count; i++)
	Java_android_atl_GskCanvas_native_1drawLine(env, this_class, snapshot_ptr, points[i + 0], points[i + 1], points[i + 2], points[i + 3], paint_ptr);
confirmed.android_behavior: In AOSP, drawLines(pts, offset, count, paint) reads one line from every 4 floats in pts[offset .. offset+count). count is the number of floats, so it draws count/4 lines. Chart libraries (MPAndroidChart grids and line charts), waveform views and games use it a lot.

Canvas.drawLines(pts) passes offset=0, count=points.length, so it draws count overlapping lines and reads 3 floats past the end of the array. The Java bounds check only covers offset+count.

confirmed.title: Matrix(Matrix src) copy constructor ignores src and returns identity

confirmed.suggested_fix: In native_create: if src is non-zero, graphene_matrix_init_from_matrix(new, src); otherwise init_identity.
confirmed.verify_reason: Matrix.c native_create ignores src and always returns identity. Matrix.java:198 passes src.native_instance into it, so new Matrix(src) never copies.

confirmed.title: Enter in EditText sends a KeyEvent with action=IME_ACTION_SEARCH(3) and actionId=0

jobject key_event = J_new__KeyEvent(env, (jlong)0, (jlong)0, IME_ACTION_SEARCH, KEYCODE_ENTER, 0, 0);
J__TextView__OnEditorActionListener__onEditorAction(env, d->listener, d->this, 0, key_event);

For the Enter key, onEditorAction gets either the IME action (e.g. IME_ACTION_SEARCH/DONE from imeOptions) or IME_NULL plus an ACTION_DOWN KEYCODE_ENTER event. confirmed.title: Dialogs always close on window close or outside tap: setCancelable is a no-op, cancel() never fires OnCancelListener

confirmed.verify_reason: Dialog.c on_close_request calls dismiss and returns FALSE. on_touch_outside calls dismiss(). Dialog.java has setCancelable{} and setOnCancelListener{} as no-ops and cancel(){dismiss();}. Dialog.java:107 defaults canceledOnTouchOutside to windowCloseOnTouchOutside=true. (AlertDialog.Builder has setCancelable/setOnCancelListener, but they end up in these no-ops.)

confirmed.title: Bitmap.setPixels/setPixel read ARGB ints as R8G8B8A8, swapping red and blue
confirmed.android_behavior: In Android, pixel ints are 0xAARRGGBB, which on little-endian are stored as bytes B,G,R,A. getPixels here downloads in GDK_MEMORY_DEFAULT (BGRA), so set and get also disagree.

confirmed.suggested_fix: Use GDK_MEMORY_B8G8R8A8 (non-premultiplied) to match Android's ARGB int layout, and download with the same format in get_pixels.
confirmed.verify_reason: native_set_pixels builds the texture with GDK_MEMORY_R8G8B8A8 from Java ARGB ints. On little-endian those bytes are B,G,R,A, so red and blue are swapped. get_pixels downloads with gdk_texture_download, which gives premultiplied BGRA, so set and get also disagree.

confirmed.title: Bitmap.getPixel()/partial getPixels() exits the whole process
confirmed.android_behavior: getPixel(x,y) returns one color, and getPixels can read any sub-rectangle. Color pickers, palette/theming code, image hit-testing and games use getPixel.

confirmed.suggested_fix: Download the full texture (or use GdkTextureDownloader) into a temp buffer and copy the requested sub-rectangle into pixels[offset + row*stride], converting to unpremultiplied ARGB.
confirmed.verify_reason: native_get_pixels calls exit(1) for any read that is not the full texture. Bitmap.getPixel calls it with a 1x1 region at (x,y), so any getPixel on a bitmap bigger than 1x1 kills the process.

confirmed.title: AssetManager.setConfiguration drops the locale, so localized resources are never selected

const struct ResTable_config config = {
	.mcc = mcc,
	.mnc = mnc,
	.orientation = orientation,
	... /* no language/country */

confirmed.title: Drawable.setLevel/getLevel are final no-ops, so level-based drawables never change

LevelListDrawable never switches (battery, signal and status icons). Ring shapes with useLevel and level-scaled gradients stay empty. Because the methods are final, subclasses cannot fix this.

Add protected boolean onLevelChange(int level) { return false; } to Drawable, then uncomment the @Override onLevelChange implementations in LayerDrawable, DrawableWrapper and ClipDrawable.
confirmed.verify_reason: Confirmed: Drawable.java lines 202-203 are final, getLevel returns 0 and setLevel returns false, and onLevelChange is never called. Downgraded to medium because <clip> and <level-list> cannot be inflated from XML anyway (finding 2), so this only matters for drawables built in code and level-scaled gradients.

confirmed.title: selectDrawable(-1) keeps showing the previous child instead of clearing it
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP DrawableContainer.selectDrawable(idx) with idx < 0 sets mCurrDrawable = null and mCurIndex = -1, so a selector whose items don't match the current state draws nothing.

confirmed.suggested_fix: When idx < 0 (or the slot is null), set curIndex = -1, call native_selectChild(paintable, 0) (and let the native side handle a NULL child), invalidateSelf(), and return true if curIndex changed.
confirmed.verify_reason: Confirmed: selectDrawable only acts when idx >= 0 and returns false otherwise, so curIndex and the native child stay on the previous drawable. StateListDrawable passes idx -1 when no item matches the state and there is no wildcard item.

confirmed.title: DrawableContainer.setBounds skips super and never gives newly selected children bounds

confirmed.impact: getBounds()/copyBounds() on any StateListDrawable, LevelListDrawable or AnimationDrawable return 0x0, which breaks compound-drawable layout and custom views that size from getBounds(). When the drawable is drawn through Java (inside a LayerDrawable, ripple, inset or custom view), a child selected after a state change keeps empty or stale bounds and draws nothing, or draws in the wrong place.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Call super.setBounds(...) (or override onBoundsChange) and, in selectDrawable, call newChild.setBounds(getBounds()), setState(getState()), setLevel(getLevel()) and copy alpha/colour filter, as AOSP does.
confirmed.verify_reason: Confirmed: DrawableContainer.setBounds does not call super, so the container's own mBounds stay empty, and selectDrawable never gives the new child bounds. This matters on the Java draw path and for getBounds() callers.

confirmed.title: StateListDrawable instances from the Resources cache share child drawables, and the container passes on no alpha, tint or filter
confirmed.android_behavior: Each new StateListDrawable gets its own child instances, created lazily from the children's ConstantStates. DrawableContainer.setAlpha, setColorFilter, setTintList and setDither apply to the current child and are remembered for children selected later.

Calling mutate().setColor() or setAlpha() on one child (Drawable.getCurrent() returns the container itself here) changes all views. setAlpha, setColorFilter and setTint on a selector do nothing because the base no-ops are not overridden.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In the copy constructor, create child copies with drawables[i].getConstantState().newDrawable(res) (or lazily). Make DrawableContainerState.newDrawable abstract or create a new container. Override setAlpha, getAlpha, setColorFilter, setTintList, setTintMode and getPadding to pass through to the current child and apply them on selection. Override getCurrent() to return the selected child.

DrawableContainer has no setAlpha, setColorFilter or setTint overrides.

confirmed.title: ColorDrawable has no setAlpha/getAlpha, and setColor neither invalidates nor reaches a View background
confirmed.android_behavior: ColorDrawable.setAlpha scales the colour's alpha and getAlpha returns it. setColor and setAlpha call invalidateSelf(), so the owning View repaints with the new colour.
confirmed.impact: Common patterns do nothing: fading a toolbar or action bar background with getBackground().setAlpha(...) on scroll, animating ((ColorDrawable) view.getBackground()).setColor(...), and ColorDrawable tinting. getAlpha() always returns 255.

Either stop special-casing ColorDrawable in View.setBackgroundDrawable, or set the callback and re-push the colour on invalidateDrawable.

confirmed.title: LayerDrawable.setColorFilter is commented out and setTintList is missing, so layer-list and ripple tints are ignored
confirmed.android_behavior: LayerDrawable passes setColorFilter, setTintList and setTintBlendMode on to every layer.

confirmed.suggested_fix: Uncomment setColorFilter and add setTintList/setTintMode overrides that loop over the children, as AOSP LayerDrawable does. Also uncomment getOpacity, setDither and setAutoMirrored.
confirmed.verify_reason: Confirmed: LayerDrawable.setColorFilter is commented out (around line 431), there is no setTintList override, and the Drawable base setTintList is empty.

confirmed.title: LayerDrawable ignores the item gravity, width, height, start and end attributes and their setters
confirmed.android_behavior: Since API 23 layer items support android:gravity, width, height, start and end (RTL-aware insets). onBoundsChange positions each layer with Gravity.apply using its width and height or intrinsic size.

Insets written with start/end (the AndroidX/Material convention) are dropped.

confirmed.verify_reason: Confirmed: inflate reads only the left, top, right, bottom, drawable and id item attributes, and setLayerWidth and setLayerGravity have empty bodies.

confirmed.title: Paint colour filter ignores the PorterDuff mode, and other ColorFilter types are dropped
confirmed.android_behavior: PorterDuffColorFilter applies the actual blend mode (MULTIPLY darkens, SRC_ATOP keeps the destination alpha, DST_IN masks, and so on). ColorMatrixColorFilter applies the 4x5 matrix, LightingColorFilter multiplies and adds, and BlendModeColorFilter (used by ShapeDrawable tint and androidx BlendModeColorFilterCompat on API 29+) blends.
confirmed.impact: MULTIPLY or SCREEN colour filters flatten images to a solid silhouette. Grayscale and saturation effects (ColorMatrix for disabled or 'read' states) and LightingColorFilter do nothing. ShapeDrawable tint (mBlendModeColorFilter) and BlendModeColorFilterCompat tints are ignored. Separately, native drawBitmap never applies paint alpha, so Paint.setAlpha fades on bitmaps do nothing.

Map ColorMatrixColorFilter to gtk_snapshot_push_color_matrix, map LightingColorFilter to a diagonal matrix plus offset, and handle BlendModeColorFilter like PorterDuff. Push an opacity node for paint->color.alpha in drawBitmap.
confirmed.verify_reason: Confirmed: native_set_color_filter builds a fixed matrix that replaces RGB with the filter colour and uses mode only as an on/off flag. The ColorMatrixColorFilter and LightingColorFilter constructors store nothing, and native drawBitmap ignores the paint alpha.

confirmed.title: Canvas.drawText(char[], index, count, ...) treats count as an end index

GskCanvas does not override this, so view drawing hits it too: custom text views, chart labels, and libraries that keep char buffers.
confirmed.suggested_fix: public void drawText(char[] text, int index, int count, float x, float y, Paint paint) { drawText(new String(text, index, count), x, y, paint); }

confirmed.title: Path.Direction is ignored, so CW/CCW sub-paths can't cut holes (GradientDrawable ring draws a filled disc)

Overlay and cut-out views (tutorial or showcase spotlights, QR scanner frames) built from addRect CW plus addCircle/addRoundRect CCW fill everything. addCircle is also only a stub.

confirmed.title: Paint text measurement returns guesses and constants although native Pango metrics exist
confirmed.android_behavior: measureText returns the shaped advance width, breakText returns how many characters fit in maxWidth and fills measuredWidth, getTextWidths fills per-character advances and returns the character count, and ascent()/descent() return font metrics (descent is positive).
confirmed.impact: Custom-drawn text in charts, badges, avatars with initials, Material chip/badge widths (TextDrawableHelper), and ellipsizing or marquee widgets is mis-sized and mis-centred. The common centring idiom y = cy - (descent()+ascent())/2 is off by about half the text height. breakText returning 10 for shorter strings leads to substring crashes, and getTextWidths leaves the array as zeros.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add a native measure based on pango_layout_get_extents (logical width) for measureText and getTextWidths (iterate clusters). Implement breakText with pango_layout_xy_to_index, or a loop over the measured widths. Derive ascent()/descent() from the existing native_get_font_metrics.
confirmed.verify_reason: Confirmed: ascent() returns -textSize, descent() returns 0, measureText(char[]) returns 10, measureText(String) uses 0.6*size per character, and every breakText overload returns 10.

confirmed.title: Typeface is fake: DEFAULT_BOLD is not bold, custom fonts load as DEFAULT, and Paint.setTypeface is a no-op
confirmed.android_behavior: Typeface objects carry family and style. DEFAULT_BOLD has getStyle()==BOLD, and MONOSPACE and SERIF are distinct families. createFromAsset/createFromFile load the font file. Paint.setTypeface changes the font used by measureText and drawText.
confirmed.impact: Text drawn on a Canvas (charts, custom views, icon fonts such as FontAwesome or Material icon fonts drawn via Paint) uses the default sans font and weight. Icon-font glyphs show as tofu or letters, and bold or monospace labels look plain. Code that checks getStyle() for bold never sees it.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Store family name and style in Typeface. Load asset and file fonts through fontconfig (FcConfigAppFontAddFile) or a Pango font map and keep the resolved family name. Have Paint.setTypeface set the family, weight and style on paint->font and remember the Typeface for getTypeface().
confirmed.verify_reason: Confirmed: every Typeface constant is create(null, 0), createFromAsset returns DEFAULT, Paint.setTypeface is a no-op, and getTypeface returns new Typeface().

confirmed.title: Paint Java/native mismatches and wrong defaults: text align, letter spacing, text scale, PathEffect, copies
confirmed.android_behavior: Defaults are Align.LEFT, letterSpacing 0, textScaleX 1.0 and strokeMiter 4, and getPathEffect() returns null until one is set. Paint(Paint) and set(Paint) copy every attribute, including shader, xfermode, colour filter and align. DashPathEffect makes dashed strokes.
confirmed.impact: getTextAlign() reports CENTER while drawing LEFT, so code that saves and restores alignment or branches on it misplaces text. Copied paints lose their xfermode (Canvas CLEAR paths) and report a null colour filter while the native copy still filters. Width maths that multiplies by getTextScaleX() gets 0, and code that adds to getLetterSpacing() doubles spacing. Dashed strokes (GradientDrawable <stroke android:dashWidth>, chart grid lines) draw solid.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Initialise align = Align.LEFT. Copy all Java fields in Paint(Paint) and set(Paint). Return 0f, 1f and 4f for letter spacing, text scale and stroke miter and store the set values. Store PathEffect, return null by default, and map DashPathEffect to gsk_stroke_set_dash in the native stroke.
confirmed.verify_reason: Confirmed: align defaults to Align.CENTER, Paint(Paint) copies only the native paint, getLetterSpacing returns 1.0f, getTextScaleX and getStrokeMiter return 0, getPathEffect returns new PathEffect(), and setPathEffect is a no-op.

confirmed.title: Canvas clip operations ignore Region.Op, and getClipBounds returns the screen size
confirmed.android_behavior: clipRect/clipPath with DIFFERENCE exclude the area (a hole), and other ops combine regions. getClipBounds returns the current clip in local coordinates: for a view's onDraw, the view's size minus any clips and translations.
confirmed.impact: DIFFERENCE clips (draw everything except a rectangle or circle: spotlight and tutorial overlays, crop and scanner frames, "excluding" clips in charts) draw only inside the hole, the exact opposite. Custom views that centre or scale content from canvas.getClipBounds() (a common onDraw idiom) lay out against the full display and draw off-centre or oversized. GskCanvas inherits both.
confirmed.suggested_fix: For DIFFERENCE, build an inverse-fill path (Path with INVERSE_WINDING) and use the existing clipPath push. Track the clip rect (intersected and transformed) in GskCanvas through save/restore, and return it from getClipBounds.
confirmed.verify_reason: Confirmed: the clipRect and clipPath overloads that take Region.Op ignore the op. getClipBounds returns the display size (marked 'UGLY HACK'), and GskCanvas does not override it.

confirmed.title: Color.colorToHSV and HSVToColor give wrong results (hue offsets and a fraction multiplied by 6)
confirmed.android_behavior: Hue is in [0,360): 60*((g-b)/d mod 6) when red is max, 60*((b-r)/d + 2) when green is max, 60*((r-g)/d + 4) when blue is max, and 0 for greys. HSVToColor uses f = h/60 - floor(h/60), in [0,1).
confirmed.impact: Green-dominant colours get a hue 120 degrees too high and blue-dominant colours a hue past 360. Reds with g<b get a negative hue, and greys get 360. HSVToColor blows up the intermediate values (q and t go negative) for any hue not on a 60-degree boundary. Apps that darken or lighten theme colours with HSV (status bar from toolbar colour, colour pickers, palette-based theming, pressed-state shades) get the wrong colours. Example: colorToHSV(0xFF00FF00) gives hue 240 (blue) instead of 120.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use the standard formulas: green branch 2 + (b-r)/d, blue branch 4 + (r-g)/d, red branch ((g-b)/d) with a negative result +6, greys hue 0. In HSVToColor, f = h/60 - floor(h/60). Also normalise h with ((h % 360) + 360) % 360.
confirmed.verify_reason: Confirmed: the green branch computes 2+x+2, the blue branch 4+x+4, greys get hue 6*60=360, and HSVToColor multiplies f by 6. The results are wrong.

confirmed.title: AnimationDrawable.inflate is commented out, and the oneShot default is true instead of false
confirmed.android_behavior: <animation-list> inflates its <item android:drawable android:duration> frames and android:oneshot. A programmatically built AnimationDrawable loops by default (mOneShot false).
confirmed.impact: Frame animations from XML (loading spinners, animated logos and avatars) are empty: getNumberOfFrames()==0 and start() shows nothing, with no error. Animations built in code with addFrame()+start() play once and stop on the last frame instead of looping.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Uncomment and adapt inflate (replace the missing inflateWithAttributes with a direct read of R.styleable.AnimationDrawable_visible/oneshot). Call it from the "animation-list" case in createFromXmlInner. Set mOneShot = false for a fresh state.
confirmed.verify_reason: Confirmed: inflate is commented out, the animation-list case returns an empty AnimationDrawable, and a fresh AnimationState sets mOneShot = true where AOSP uses false.

confirmed.title: Bitmap.compress(JPEG/WEBP) writes the text 'fixme Bitmap.compress JPEG' into the output stream
confirmed.android_behavior: Encodes the bitmap as JPEG or WEBP at the given quality into the stream and returns true.
confirmed.impact: Apps that save photos, thumbnails, cropped avatars, screenshots or share images as JPEG (the most common format) write a corrupt file containing that string. Many ignore the return value, so later loads fail or the corrupt file is shared. Image caches (e.g. disk caches using JPEG) fill with garbage.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Encode JPEG through gdk-pixbuf (gdk_pixbuf_save_to_buffer with "jpeg" and a quality option) or libjpeg. For WEBP use libwebp, or fall back to PNG while still returning a valid image. Never write placeholder bytes into the caller's stream.
confirmed.verify_reason: Confirmed: for any format other than PNG, compress writes the bytes 'fixme Bitmap.compress <FORMAT>' into the caller's stream and returns false.

confirmed.title: GradientDrawable reduces solid and stroke ColorStateLists to one colour and never reacts to state; sweep gradients are commented out
confirmed.android_behavior: Since API 21, <solid android:color> and <stroke android:color> accept ColorStateLists. GradientDrawable is stateful when they (or the tint) are stateful, and updates the paint colours in onStateChange. Sweep gradients render a conic gradient.
confirmed.impact: Shapes using colour selectors (@color/btn_bg_selector with state_enabled/pressed/checked, common for outlined and filled buttons and chips) are stuck on the default colour. backgroundTint selectors on <shape> backgrounds never change with state. Sweep-gradient shapes render solid black (see the shader finding).
confirmed.suggested_fix: Read the colours with a.getColorStateList, store the ColorStateLists in GradientState, add setColor(ColorStateList)/setStroke(int, ColorStateList), and implement isStateful() and onStateChange() to re-resolve the solid, stroke and tint colours. Restore the sweep branch once shaders are implemented.
confirmed.verify_reason: Confirmed: solid and stroke colours are read with a.getColor, and GradientDrawable has no isStateful or onStateChange. The sweep gradient branch is commented out.

confirmed.title: StateListDrawable inflates items without the theme, so ?attr references in selector items don't resolve
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP StateListDrawable.inflateChildElements uses obtainAttributes(r, theme, attrs, R.styleable.StateListDrawableItem), so items like android:drawable="?attr/selectableItemBackground" or "?attr/colorAccent" resolve against the current theme.
confirmed.impact: Selectors whose items point at theme attributes (very common in AppCompat and Material themes and app styles) get null or unresolved drawables. That item then has no drawable or throws 'requires a drawable attribute', so themed pressed and checked states or whole backgrounds go missing.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use Drawable.obtainAttributes(r, theme, attrs, ...) (the helper already exists in Drawable) for both TypedArrays, as LayerDrawable and GradientDrawable already do.
confirmed.verify_reason: Confirmed: StateListDrawable uses r.obtainAttributes(attrs, ...) without the theme, and Resources.obtainAttributes calls retrieveAttributes with no theme, so ?attr references cannot resolve. The Drawable.obtainAttributes(r, theme, ...) helper exists but is not used here.

confirmed.title: setBackgroundDrawable ignores the drawable's padding and state, and ColorDrawable backgrounds skip callback and tint
confirmed.android_behavior: In AOSP, setBackgroundDrawable (1) applies the drawable's getPadding() as view padding when the view has no explicit padding (9-patch content area, InsetDrawable, layer-list padding), (2) calls setState(getDrawableState()) for stateful drawables, (3) sets the callback on every drawable, including ColorDrawable, and clears it on the old one, and (4) applies the background tint list/mode to every drawable type.
confirmed.impact: Buttons and EditTexts with 9-patch or inset backgrounds lose their built-in content padding. A selector set on an already activated or selected view shows the default state. For ColorDrawable backgrounds (android:background="#..."), the common 'toolbar.getBackground().setAlpha(a)' fade-on-scroll and getBackground().setColor() do nothing, and android:backgroundTint on a colour background is ignored.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Mirror AOSP: clear the old drawable's callback; always setCallback(this); if isStateful(), setState(getDrawableState()); apply the tint to ColorDrawable too, or route ColorDrawable through the paintable path so invalidation works; and if drawable.getPadding(rect) returns true and no user padding was set, call setPadding from the rect.
confirmed.verify_reason: The code at 1951-1962 matches the quote. ColorDrawable returns early with the colour baked in natively: no callback and no tint, so a later setAlpha/setColor on getBackground() has no effect. getPadding() is never used in View.java. The state is set only later through drawableStateChanged, not when the background is set. The padding loss is the most visible effect.

confirmed.title: ViewGroup.offsetChildrenTopAndBottom is an empty FIXME, but GridView depends on it
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP offsets every child's top and bottom by `offset` (child.offsetTopAndBottom). AbsListView/GridView use it to correct gaps after filling and to scroll.
confirmed.impact: In GridView-based screens (galleries, launchers, icon pickers, older apps), the post-fill corrections (correctTooHigh/correctTooLow, adjustViewsUpOrDown) and keyboard/position scrolling do nothing. Rows overlap or leave gaps, and selection scrolling breaks.
confirmed.suggested_fix: for (View child : children) child.offsetTopAndBottom(offset); then invalidate().
confirmed.verify_reason: ViewGroup.java 622-624 is an empty FIXME, and the widget code calls offsetChildrenTopAndBottom about 15 times (GridView/AbsListView).

confirmed.title: withEndAction/withStartAction are never cleared and re-run on every later animate() call
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP attaches start/end actions to the single animation being started; they run once and are not inherited by the next animate() call. The end action also does not run when the animation is cancelled.
confirmed.impact: The common 'animate().alpha(0).withEndAction(() -> v.setVisibility(GONE))' followed later by 'animate().alpha(1)' runs the old GONE action again, and the view disappears after fading in. Cancelling also triggers the end action. Visible in show/hide toggles, toasts and snackbars.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Capture startAction/endAction in local variables in start(), set the fields to null, attach them only to that animator, and skip endAction when the animation was cancelled.
confirmed.verify_reason: View.animate() returns one cached ViewPropertyAnimator (2109-2112). start() never clears startAction/endAction, so later animate() calls attach the old actions again. animator.cancel() in start() also ends the previous animation, which can fire its end listener.

confirmed.title: Focus-change and key listeners are dropped: setOnFocusChangeListener/setOnKeyListener are empty, OnFocusChangeListener has no method, and dispatchKeyEvent ignores listeners and onKeyUp
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP calls OnKeyListener.onKey first, then KeyEvent.dispatch → onKeyDown/onKeyUp. OnFocusChangeListener.onFocusChange(View, boolean) fires on every focus change. getOnFocusChangeListener() returns the listener.
confirmed.impact: On a desktop with a keyboard, 'press Enter in this EditText to submit' via setOnKeyListener does nothing, and onKeyUp overrides (for example the Back/Menu handling in many custom views) never run. Form validation on blur, show-keyboard-on-focus and focus highlighting through OnFocusChangeListener never fire. getOnFocusChangeListener() returns null after a set.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Declare onFocusChange(View v, boolean hasFocus) in the interface, store the listener and call it from the GTK focus-enter/leave path. Store the OnKeyListener, call it in dispatchKeyEvent before onKeyDown, and dispatch ACTION_UP to onKeyUp.
confirmed.verify_reason: setOnFocusChangeListener (2224) and setOnKeyListener (1407) are empty. The OnFocusChangeListener interface (733) has no method. getOnFocusChangeListener returns null. dispatchKeyEvent (2667) handles only ACTION_DOWN through onKeyDown. No widget overrides add listener support.

confirmed.title: <include> ignores android:visibility (and other overrides besides id and layout_*) on the include tag
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP's parseInclude reads View_id and View_visibility from the include tag and applies both to the included root (VISIBLE/INVISIBLE/GONE).
confirmed.impact: The very common '<include layout="@layout/empty_state" android:visibility="gone"/>' (also used for loading/error overlays) is shown at startup, overlapping real content until code hides it.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Also read com.android.internal.R.attr.visibility from the include attrs and call view.setVisibility(VISIBILITY_FLAGS[value]) when it is present.
confirmed.verify_reason: parseInclude (LayoutInflater 349-355) reads only id from the include attrs (plus layout params); visibility is never applied.

confirmed.title: Window.addFlags/setFlags/clearFlags are empty: FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON, FLAG_FULLSCREEN and others are ignored and not reflected in getAttributes()
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP updates mWindowAttributes.flags and applies them. FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON (0x80) keeps the display awake and FLAG_FULLSCREEN (0x400) hides the status bar. The constant is 128, not 0. The 5-argument LayoutParams constructor stores type, flags and format.
confirmed.impact: Video players, games, navigation, recipe and timer apps call getWindow().addFlags(FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON). The screen still blanks, even though ATL already has native_keep_screen_on for View.setKeepScreenOn. Games that use FLAG_FULLSCREEN do not go fullscreen. getAttributes().flags reads back 0, and popup windows lose their type and flags.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep params.flags = (params.flags & ~mask) | (flags & mask). Map the 0x80 bit to native_keep_screen_on on the decor view and 0x400 to nativeSetFullscreen. Fix FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON to 0x80 and store type/flags/format in the LayoutParams constructor.
confirmed.verify_reason: Window.java 56-58: addFlags/setFlags/clearFlags are empty. WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON = 0, and the 5-argument constructor discards type/flags/format.

confirmed.title: scrollTo/setScrollX/setScrollY never call onScrollChanged or the scroll-change listener (setOnScrollChangeListener is empty)
confirmed.android_behavior: In AOSP, scrollTo only acts when the position changes; it then calls onScrollChanged(x, y, oldX, oldY), notifies the OnScrollChangeListener and invalidates. setScrollX/Y go through scrollTo.
confirmed.impact: Custom views and libraries that override onScrollChanged (parallax headers, ScrollView subclasses, sticky headers, scroll-to-hide toolbars), and apps using View.setOnScrollChangeListener, get no callbacks. setScrollX/Y also do not redraw.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In scrollTo: if (x != scrollX || y != scrollY) { int ox = scrollX, oy = scrollY; scrollX = x; scrollY = y; onScrollChanged(x, y, ox, oy); if (on_scroll_change_listener != null) on_scroll_change_listener.onScrollChange(this, x, y, ox, oy); invalidate(); }. Store the listener in the setter and route setScrollX/Y through scrollTo.
confirmed.verify_reason: scrollTo (1643) only sets the fields and invalidates. onScrollChanged is never called, setOnScrollChangeListener (1361) is empty, and setScrollX/Y (2768) only set the fields with no invalidate. No subclass overrides scrollTo.

confirmed.title: setBackgroundTintList/Mode are empty and getBackgroundTintList returns null; the XML backgroundTint keeps only the default colour
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP stores the ColorStateList and mode and applies them to the background drawable through setTintList/setTintMode, so the tint follows state (pressed/disabled/checked). ViewCompat.setBackgroundTintList calls this directly on API 21+.
confirmed.impact: Programmatic background tints (status chips, coloured buttons, category labels, 'view.setBackgroundTintList(ColorStateList.valueOf(color))') have no effect: views keep the base drawable colour. XML state-list tints lose their disabled and pressed colours.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep a ColorStateList field and PorterDuff.Mode, apply them with background.setTintList/setTintMode in setBackgroundDrawable and the setters, read View_backgroundTint with getColorStateList, and return the stored values from the getters.
confirmed.verify_reason: setBackgroundTintList/Mode are empty and the getters return null. Only an int backgroundTint from XML is applied in setBackgroundDrawable, and it is skipped for ColorDrawable.

confirmed.title: Focus queries return constants: hasFocus() is false, findFocus() returns this, clearFocus() is a no-op
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP: hasFocus() is true if this view or a descendant has focus. findFocus() returns the focused view in the subtree or null. clearFocus() removes focus and calls the focus-change listener.
confirmed.impact: 'Hide keyboard on outside tap' code (if (!editText.hasFocus()) ..., view.findFocus() then hideSoftInputFromWindow) and search-bar collapse logic misbehave. findFocus() returning a non-focused root makes ScrollView/RecyclerView scroll to the wrong view. clearFocus() on an EditText leaves the cursor in it.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Implement hasFocus() via nativeIsFocused on this view plus any descendant (GTK focus-within). findFocus() should return the focused descendant or null, and clearFocus() should move GTK focus away (gtk_widget_grab_focus on the root or gtk_root_set_focus(NULL)).
confirmed.verify_reason: hasFocus() returns false (2097), findFocus() returns this (2330), and clearFocus() is empty (2199). No overrides in the widgets.

confirmed.title: isLaidOut() always returns true and isShown() always returns true
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP isLaidOut() is false until the first layout pass since the last attach. isShown() is false when this view or any ancestor is not VISIBLE, or when it is not attached to a window.
confirmed.impact: ViewCompat.isLaidOut drives BottomSheetBehavior, CoordinatorLayout behaviours, ViewPager2 and the doOnLayout/doOnPreDraw KTX helpers. Returning true before layout makes them use zero sizes (bottom sheets at the wrong offset, zero-width animations). isShown() is used to decide whether to play animations, show tooltips or count impressions; hidden views are treated as visible.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Track a laid-out flag set in layoutInternal/layout() and cleared on detach. For isShown(), walk the parents checking visibility == VISIBLE and that the last parent is the window (isAttachedToWindow()).
confirmed.verify_reason: isLaidOut() (2287) and isShown() (2324) return true unconditionally, with no overrides. AndroidX uses ViewCompat.isLaidOut/doOnLayout for deferred work.

confirmed.title: getScaledVerticalScrollFactor()/HorizontalScrollFactor return 1 pixel per wheel unit
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP returns about 64dp in pixels (config_verticalScrollFactor / listPreferredItemHeightSmall), the distance one wheel notch scrolls.
confirmed.impact: ATL delivers mouse wheel events as ACTION_SCROLL (android_view_View.c). RecyclerView, NestedScrollView and Compose multiply AXIS_VSCROLL by ViewConfigurationCompat.getScaledVerticalScrollFactor(), which calls this on API 26+, so a wheel notch scrolls about 1 px. Lists are effectively unscrollable with a mouse wheel on desktop.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Return 64 * displayMetrics.density for both factors, using the context passed to get(); keep the ViewConfiguration instance per context.
confirmed.verify_reason: Both scroll factors return 1. scroll_cb passes wheel units through unscaled (AXIS_VSCROLL is about 1 per notch). ATL's own AbsListView hard-codes *100 to work around this, which suggests consumers that use the factor (RecyclerView/NestedScrollView on API 26+) scroll about 1px per notch.

confirmed.title: View animations (Alpha/Translate/Rotate/Scale/AnimationSet, AnimationUtils.loadAnimation) never touch the view, not even the end state
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP applies the Transformation (alpha and matrix) to the view each frame. With fillAfter it keeps the final state, and AnimationSet combines its children.
confirmed.impact: Apps that use legacy view animations with fillAfter=true for real state changes (fade-out-and-stay, slide panels off screen, R.anim shake on error) show nothing; content that should vanish stays on screen. loadInterpolator returning null silently turns curves linear.
confirmed.suggested_fix: At minimum, store from/to values in Alpha/Translate/Scale/Rotate and AnimationSet. Drive them with a ValueAnimator over getDuration() that applies them to view alpha and translation through View.startAnimation, and honour fillAfter. Make loadAnimation/loadInterpolator parse the XML (alpha, translate, scale, rotate, set).
confirmed.verify_reason: Animation.start only calls the empty applyTransformation(1). AlphaAnimation stores nothing. loadAnimation returns a bare Animation and loadInterpolator returns null. View.startAnimation never applies a transformation, so fillAfter end states are never applied.

confirmed.title: CompoundButton.getText() returns the literal "FIXME CompoundButton.getText()"
confirmed.android_behavior: Returns the label text of the checkbox, radio button or switch.
confirmed.impact: Apps that read a selected RadioButton's label (for example ((RadioButton)findViewById(group.getCheckedRadioButtonId())).getText()) get a garbage string, and it can end up in saved data or on screen. RadioGroup.isVisibleWithText also uses it.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Read the label back from the native widget (gtk_check_button_get_label, or the GtkLabel in the switch box), or store the text in Java inside setText.
confirmed.verify_reason: CompoundButton.getText returns the literal "FIXME CompoundButton.getText()", and CheckBox, RadioButton and Switch do not override it.

confirmed.title: TextView typeface is ignored: setTypeface(Typeface) is empty, setTypeface(tf, style) ignores tf, and getTypeface() returns null
confirmed.android_behavior: setTypeface(Typeface.DEFAULT_BOLD / MONOSPACE / a custom font) changes the font. setTypeface(getTypeface(), Typeface.BOLD) keeps the family and adds a style. android:fontFamily and textAppearance fonts are applied.
confirmed.impact: Bold set from code (setTypeface(Typeface.DEFAULT_BOLD), extremely common for headings and selected items), monospace code views and custom fonts all render as regular sans. Toggling bold off with setTypeface(Typeface.DEFAULT) leaves it bold, because the CSS class is only removed in the two-argument variant.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Implement setTypeface(Typeface) by deriving the style from tf.getStyle() and the family from tf. Store and return the typeface.
confirmed.verify_reason: setTypeface(Typeface) is empty and getTypeface returns null. setTypeface(tf, style) only toggles the bold/italic CSS classes and ignores tf. setTypeface(DEFAULT_BOLD) and monospace fonts are lost.

confirmed.title: SeekBar listener fires start/changed/stop on every change-value, before the value is applied, and never for programmatic setProgress
confirmed.android_behavior: onStartTrackingTouch fires once at touch down and onStopTrackingTouch once at release. onProgressChanged fires with the clamped value after it is applied, so getProgress() matches, and setProgress from code fires onProgressChanged(fromUser=false).
confirmed.impact: Media players that seek on onStopTrackingTouch seek on every pixel of drag, which stutters audio and video. GTK's change-value value can be outside the range (GTK docs), and seekBar.getProgress() inside onProgressChanged returns the previous value. UI that is kept in sync through onProgressChanged after setProgress never updates.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use the GtkGestureDrag/click begin and end on the scale for start and stop tracking, the value-changed signal for onProgressChanged (clamp the value, and track fromUser with a flag set inside change-value), and fire onProgressChanged(false) from setProgress.
confirmed.verify_reason: on_change_value in android_widget_SeekBar.c calls start, changed(fromUser=TRUE) and stop on every change-value signal, which runs before the value is applied. getProgress reads the GtkRange value, so it still holds the old value. Java setProgress fires no listener.

confirmed.title: CheckedTextView does not implement Checkable; setChecked is empty and no checkmark is drawn
confirmed.android_behavior: CheckedTextView implements Checkable and draws checkMark. ListView CHOICE_MODE_SINGLE/MULTIPLE (simple_list_item_single_choice / multiple_choice) calls ((Checkable)child).setChecked(...) to show the selection, and AlertDialog setSingleChoiceItems relies on it.
confirmed.impact: Single- and multiple-choice lists and dialogs (settings pickers, sort-by dialogs) show no selection state. ListView's `child instanceof Checkable` check fails, so it falls back to setActivated. Code calling isChecked() fails with NoSuchMethodError.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Implement Checkable (store mChecked, refreshDrawableState with state_checked, and isChecked/toggle), read android:checked and checkMark, and render the checkmark as a compound drawable.
confirmed.verify_reason: CheckedTextView extends TextView only and does not implement Checkable. setChecked and setCheckMarkDrawable are empty. ATL's ListView and AbsListView use 'child instanceof Checkable' to show choice state, so that check fails.

confirmed.title: RadioButton.setText(CharSequence) is native but the C side treats it as jstring
confirmed.android_behavior: setText accepts any CharSequence: String, SpannedString from getText(resId) or styled string resources, SpannableString, Html.fromHtml.
confirmed.impact: Passing a non-String CharSequence (getText(R.string.x) when the resource has styling, Html.fromHtml, SpannableString, or the XML text attribute that TextView's constructor passes on through a.getText) calls GetStringUTFChars on a non-String object. That is undefined behaviour: garbage labels or a JNI abort.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make the Java side call a private native_setText(String) with text == null ? "" : text.toString(), as CheckBox does.
confirmed.verify_reason: RadioButton declares 'public native void setText(CharSequence)', and the C side calls GetStringUTFChars on it as a jstring. A non-String CharSequence (styled getText, SpannableString, fromHtml) reaches it through virtual dispatch from the TextView and Button constructors and from setText(int).

confirmed.title: ScrollView: fillViewport ignored, fullScroll returns true without scrolling, scrollTo/smoothScrollTo do not move the GtkScrolledWindow
confirmed.android_behavior: android:fillViewport="true" stretches the child to the viewport height, which is very common for forms and login screens with bottom-aligned buttons. fullScroll(FOCUS_DOWN) and scrollTo/smoothScrollTo move the scroll position (chat logs, terminal output, jumping to an error field), and getScrollY reflects the user's scroll.
confirmed.impact: Screens built on fillViewport collapse to content height and lose bottom alignment. Log and chat views never auto-scroll to the end. Scroll position save and restore does not work.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Read ScrollView_fillViewport and measure the child with EXACTLY viewport height when it is smaller. Implement scrollTo/fullScroll/smoothScrollTo by setting the GtkAdjustment of the scrolled window, and update scrollX/scrollY from its value-changed signal.
confirmed.verify_reason: setFillViewport is empty and fullScroll returns true without doing anything. ScrollView.c has only the constructor, addView and removeView, with no adjustment handling. The scrollTo part is less certain: WrapperWidget offsets the allocation by getScrollX, so View.scrollTo may have some visual effect. The fillViewport and fullScroll parts hold.

confirmed.title: HorizontalScrollView is a plain FrameLayout with no native scroller
confirmed.android_behavior: Measures its child with an UNSPECIFIED width and lets the user scroll horizontally. Used for chip and tag rows, toolbars of formatting buttons, and wide tables.
confirmed.impact: Wide rows are squeezed to the screen width or clipped, and content past the right edge cannot be reached. smoothScrollTo is a no-op.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Mirror ScrollView: a native GtkScrolledWindow with a horizontal policy, an onMeasure that measures the child with an UNSPECIFIED width, and scrollTo/smoothScrollTo mapped to the hadjustment.
confirmed.verify_reason: HorizontalScrollView is a bare FrameLayout subclass with no native constructor, no onMeasure override and empty smoothScrollTo and setFillViewport.

confirmed.title: Button/EditText/CompoundButton override setTextSize (and CompoundButton setTextColor) with empty bodies
confirmed.android_behavior: Buttons, inputs, checkboxes and switches honour android:textSize and textColor from XML and from code.
confirmed.impact: android:textSize on buttons and edit fields is ignored, because the TextView constructor calls the overridden setTextSize. Calculator keypads, large-number inputs and small chip buttons render at the default size, and checkbox or switch label colours stay at the default (unreadable on custom backgrounds).
