confirmed.suggested_fix: Apply the size and colour through a Pango attribute or CSS on the inner GtkLabel/GtkText for each widget type instead of discarding them.
confirmed.verify_reason: Button, EditText, CompoundButton, CheckBox and RadioButton all override setTextSize(float) with empty bodies. The colour claim is partly wrong: XML textColor goes through setTextColor(ColorStateList), which calls native_setTextColor (CSS on the widget), so only setTextColor(int) from code is dropped on compound buttons.

confirmed.title: Button.setText(null) shows "null"; Button and EditText don't override setText(CharSequence, BufferType), so that path writes into the wrong native widget
confirmed.android_behavior: setText(null) clears the text. setText(text, BufferType.EDITABLE/SPANNABLE) sets the text on any TextView subclass.
confirmed.impact: Buttons fed a null string literally read "null". editText.setText(str, TextView.BufferType.EDITABLE), a common idiom, runs TextView's native_setText, whose box_get_label walks the children of a GtkText or GtkButton instead of the label box. The text is not set, and GTK prints criticals or crashes.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use text == null ? "" : text.toString() in Button, and override setText(CharSequence, BufferType) in Button, EditText and CompoundButton to route to their own native setters.
confirmed.verify_reason: Button.setText uses String.valueOf(text), so null becomes "null". Button and EditText do not override setText(CharSequence, BufferType), so that path calls TextView.native_setText. Its box_get_label runs on the GtkButton or GtkText, whose last child is not a label, and ends with GTK_LABEL(NULL or a box), which gives criticals and the text is not set.

confirmed.title: TextWatcher callbacks are wrong: beforeTextChanged never fires, and onTextChanged gets start=0,before=0,count=UTF-8 byte length
confirmed.android_behavior: beforeTextChanged(s, start, count, after) fires first, then onTextChanged(s, start, before, count) with the char range that changed, then afterTextChanged with the live Editable.
confirmed.impact: Watchers that use start/before/count (mention pickers, character-limited fields, undo, autocomplete triggers on the typed char) get bogus ranges. strlen counts bytes, so any non-ASCII text overruns the CharSequence and throws IndexOutOfBounds. Logic that relies on beforeTextChanged never runs.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Hook GtkEditable insert-text/delete-text to compute the char offsets, call beforeTextChanged before the change and onTextChanged after it with correct ranges, and pass a live Editable to afterTextChanged.
confirmed.verify_reason: changed_cb calls onTextChanged(s, 0, 0, strlen(text)) with a UTF-8 byte count. beforeTextChanged is never called, and afterTextChanged gets a detached copy.

confirmed.title: Dialog ignores themeResId; getContext() is not wrapped in the dialog theme
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP Dialog wraps the context in a ContextThemeWrapper using themeResId, or android:dialogTheme when it is 0. getContext(), the window and the content inflation all use that dialog theme, so windowIsFloating, windowMinWidth and alert styling come from it.
confirmed.impact: Dialog content is inflated with the Activity theme. windowIsFloating is read from the activity theme (usually false), so dialogs are sized like full windows instead of floating, and AppCompat/Material dialogs (AppCompatDialog relies on Dialog's themed getContext()) get activity colors and styles instead of alertDialogTheme.
confirmed.suggested_fix: If themeResId==0, resolve android.R.attr.dialogTheme from context.getTheme(). Then set this.context = new ContextThemeWrapper(context, themeResId) before creating the Window, as AOSP does.
confirmed.verify_reason: The Dialog(Context, int themeResId) constructor ignores themeResId and stores the raw context. show() reads windowIsFloating and windowMinWidth from that context's theme. AppCompatDialog passes its resolved theme id to super and relies on Dialog's themed getContext(), so the dialog theme is lost. Severity lowered to medium because ATL's sizing logic still works for full-window dialogs.

confirmed.title: Intent copy constructor and putExtras alias Bundles instead of copying/merging; copies drop flags/type/package
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP copies extras (new Bundle(o.mExtras)) and copies flags, type, package, categories, selector and clipData. putExtras merges with mExtras.putAll(), keeping existing extras. getExtras() returns a copy, or null when there are no extras.
confirmed.impact: putExtra(...) followed by putExtras(bundle) loses the earlier extras. Later putExtra calls write into the caller's Bundle, and modifying a copied Intent mutates the original. new Intent(other) loses FLAG_ACTIVITY_* flags and the MIME type. Wrong data is passed between activities, services and PendingIntents.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Copy constructor: this.extras = o.extras != null ? new Bundle(o.extras) : null, and copy flags, type, packageName, selector and categories. putExtras: extras.putAll(src). getExtras: return a copy.
confirmed.verify_reason: The copy constructor (line 498) copies only action, data, the extras reference and component. The flags, type, packageName and selector fields exist but are not copied. Both putExtras overloads replace this.extras instead of merging and are marked FIXME HACK, so earlier extras are lost and Bundles end up shared between Intents.

confirmed.title: Context.getColor/getColorStateList resolve without the context theme
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP Context.getColor(id) is getResources().getColor(id, getTheme()) and getColorStateList(id) is getResources().getColorStateList(id, getTheme()). ContextCompat.getColor uses these on API 23+.
confirmed.impact: Color resources defined as selectors that reference ?attr (common in Material/AppCompat apps, e.g. res/color/*.xml using ?attr/colorPrimary or colorOnSurface) are inflated without a theme. ColorStateList inflation then falls back to Color.MAGENTA, so text and icons come out magenta or with unresolved colors.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pass getTheme() in both methods (getColor(resId, getTheme()), getColorStateList(id, getTheme())).
confirmed.verify_reason: Context.getColor(resId) calls getResources().getColor(resId), which becomes getColor(id, null), and getColorStateList does the same. Nothing in ContextImpl or ContextWrapper overrides them. ColorStateList inflation extracts the theme attributes and then calls a.getColor(..., Color.MAGENTA), so ?attr colors resolved without a theme come out magenta.

confirmed.title: Drawable caches' shouldInvalidateEntry throws, so Resources.updateConfiguration crashes after drawables are cached
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP returns Configuration.needNewResources(configChanges, entry.getChangingConfigurations()) and prunes only the affected entries.
confirmed.impact: ThemedResourceCache.prune calls shouldInvalidateEntry on every live entry when configChanges != 0. Apps with an in-app language or font-size picker that call resources.updateConfiguration(config, metrics) (still widespread) get UnsupportedOperationException as soon as any drawable is cached.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Implement both overrides as `return Configuration.needNewResources(configChanges, entry.getChangingConfigurations());` (as ConfigurationBoundResourceCache already does).
confirmed.verify_reason: Both ThemedResourceCache overrides (Resources.java:113 and :124) throw UnsupportedOperationException. updateConfiguration calls onConfigurationChange, which prunes; pruneEntryLocked calls shouldInvalidateEntry for every live entry when configChanges != 0. A real config change (locale or fontScale) after any drawable is cached throws.

confirmed.title: Configuration.setLocales commented out, getLocales ignores the config, default locale hard-coded en_US
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP setLocales updates locale and the layout direction, and getLocales returns the configuration's list. setToDefaults leaves the locale empty, so Resources.updateConfiguration fills it from Locale.getDefault().
confirmed.impact: The modern in-app language switch (config.setLocales(...); createConfigurationContext / AppCompatDelegate.setApplicationLocales) does nothing. Because setToDefaults forces en_US, the `if (locale == null) locale = Locale.getDefault()` branch in Resources.updateConfiguration never runs: String.format and plural rules always use en_US regardless of the user's LANG.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Restore the mLocaleList logic in setLocales/getLocales. Have setToDefaults leave locale null (or set it to Locale.getDefault()) so the system locale is used.
confirmed.verify_reason: setLocales has its body commented out, and getLocales returns LocaleList.getDefault(). setToDefaults hard-codes locale en_US, and mConfiguration is a new Configuration(), so the 'locale == null -> Locale.getDefault()' branches in updateConfiguration never run. The configuration locale is therefore always en_US.

confirmed.title: setResult delivers onActivityResult immediately and repeatedly; finishing without setResult never delivers RESULT_CANCELED
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP records the result and delivers it once, after the child finishes and before the caller's onResume. If the child finishes (e.g. Back) without setResult, the caller gets RESULT_CANCELED with null data.
confirmed.impact: onActivityResult runs while the child is still on screen and runs once per setResult call (apps often set a default result in onCreate and update it later). Back-out cancellations never reach the caller, so pickers and settings or login flows started with startActivityForResult or the AndroidX ActivityResult API can hang waiting.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Store the result code and data on the child and deliver once in finish/destroy (RESULT_CANCELED by default), posting to the caller's looper before it resumes.
confirmed.verify_reason: setResult (Activity.java:371) calls resultActivity.onActivityResult right away, on every call. finish() only posts nativeFinish, and nothing delivers RESULT_CANCELED when a child finishes without a result.

confirmed.title: Application.registerActivityLifecycleCallbacks is an empty no-op
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP dispatches onActivityCreated/Started/Resumed/Paused/Stopped/SaveInstanceState/Destroyed (and Pre/Post variants) to app-level callbacks for every activity.
confirmed.impact: AndroidX ProcessLifecycleOwner (attached through app-level callbacks) never moves past CREATED, so apps and libraries that detect foreground/background through it think the app is always in the background. Crash reporters, analytics-free foreground trackers, theme/locale helpers and passcode-lock libraries that hook every activity this way silently do nothing.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep a list in Application and have Activity's dispatch points (onCreate/onStart/.../onDestroy and the existing dispatchActivityPost*/Pre* helpers) also invoke the application's callbacks, including onActivityPreCreated.
confirmed.verify_reason: Application.registerActivityLifecycleCallbacks and unregisterActivityLifecycleCallbacks (line 125) are empty. Only Activity-level callbacks exist (Activity.java:621 onward). ProcessLifecycleOwner and similar code register on the Application, so they get nothing.

confirmed.title: Dialog setCancelable/setOnCancelListener ignored; cancel() never calls OnCancelListener; onCreate re-run on every show()
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP stores the cancel listener and calls it from cancel() (Back/outside touch), honours setCancelable(false), and calls onCreate only once per dialog (mCreated), with onStart/onStop around show/dismiss.
confirmed.impact: Apps that stop work or reset state in onCancel (ProgressDialog with a running task, confirmation flows) never get the callback. Non-cancelable dialogs are not enforced. A dialog shown a second time re-runs onCreate, re-inflating content and duplicating listeners.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Store the cancelable flag and OnCancelListener, and make cancel() invoke the listener and then dismiss(). Guard onCreate with a created flag.
confirmed.verify_reason: setCancelable and setOnCancelListener in Dialog.java (around line 81) are empty, and cancel() just calls dismiss(). show() calls onCreate(null) every time with no created guard. AlertDialog does not override any of these.

confirmed.title: IntentFilter.match discards the action-mismatch result
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP returns NO_MATCH_ACTION as soon as the action does not match, and a filter that declares data schemes does not match an intent with no data.
confirmed.impact: Context.resolveActivityInternal (used from native to resolve incoming intents) scores every filter as a positive match when the intent has no data. Any activity with any intent-filter can be picked regardless of action, so the wrong activity opens.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Return -3 right after the failed action check. When scheme==null and the filter has data schemes, return NO_MATCH_DATA. Check categories too.
confirmed.verify_reason: IntentFilter.match sets ret = -3 when the action does not match, but the following if/else unconditionally overwrites ret, so with scheme==null the result is always a positive MATCH_CATEGORY_EMPTY. Context.resolveActivityInternal (line 427) takes the first score > 0, so the action is effectively ignored for intents without data.

confirmed.title: AlarmManager.cancel is a no-op, re-setting an alarm adds duplicates, setAlarmClock does nothing
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP cancel() removes matching alarms. set*/setRepeating with an equal PendingIntent replaces the existing alarm. setAlarmClock schedules an exact alarm.
confirmed.impact: Reminder and alarm apps that reschedule on each launch or edit fire the same alarm several times. Cancelled or disabled alarms (including repeating ones, which re-post forever) still fire. Alarm-clock apps using setAlarmClock never ring.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep a map from PendingIntent (filterEquals) to the posted Runnable. Remove it in cancel() and before re-scheduling. Implement setAlarmClock as setExact(RTC_WAKEUP, info.getTriggerTime(), operation).
confirmed.verify_reason: Both cancel overloads only log. setInexactRepeating and setExact post fresh runnables with no tracking, so there is nothing cancel() could remove, and a repeating alarm re-posts itself forever. setAlarmClock has an empty body.

confirmed.title: sendBroadcast delivers synchronously on the caller's thread; receivers keyed by IntentFilter instance
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP delivers broadcasts asynchronously on the main thread (or the Handler given to registerReceiver), never inside sendBroadcast. Each registerReceiver call is a separate registration.
confirmed.impact: A broadcast sent from a worker thread runs receivers off the UI thread, so view or GTK updates race and crash. Re-entrant sends run inside the sender's stack. Registering two receivers with the same IntentFilter object silently drops the first.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Store a list of (receiver, filter, handler) registrations and post onReceive to the registration's handler, or to the main looper.
confirmed.verify_reason: sendBroadcast iterates a static Map<IntentFilter, BroadcastReceiver> and calls onReceive synchronously on the caller's thread. IntentFilter does not override equals or hashCode, so keys are by identity, and a second receiver registered with the same filter object replaces the first. The registerReceiver overload that takes a Handler ignores the scheduler.

confirmed.title: Service.stopSelf does nothing; IntentService runs onHandleIntent on the main thread
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP stopSelf() stops the service and calls onDestroy. IntentService runs onHandleIntent on a worker HandlerThread and stops itself when the queue is empty.
confirmed.impact: Services never get onDestroy, so wake locks, foreground notifications, sockets and players are never released. IntentService work (downloads, syncs, DB imports) blocks the UI thread and freezes the window.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Have stopSelf() call get_atl_loaded_app().stopService(new Intent().setComponent(component)). Port AOSP IntentService (HandlerThread + ServiceHandler + stopSelf(startId)).
confirmed.verify_reason: stopSelf, stopSelf(int) and stopSelfResult only print. IntentService.onStartCommand calls onHandleIntent directly, and ATLLoadedApp.startService calls onStartCommand from a runnable posted to the UI thread, so the work runs on the main thread.

confirmed.title: openFileOutput ignores MODE_APPEND; fileList() always empty
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP opens with append=(mode & MODE_APPEND)!=0 in getFilesDir() (creating it), and fileList() lists getFilesDir().
confirmed.impact: Apps that append logs, history or journals with MODE_APPEND truncate the file on every write and lose data. The files dir is not created first, so the first write can throw FileNotFoundException. Apps enumerating saved files with fileList() see none.
confirmed.suggested_fix: return new FileOutputStream(new File(getFilesDir(), name), (mode & 0x8000) != 0); and fileList(): String[] l = getFilesDir().list(); return l != null ? l : new String[0];
confirmed.verify_reason: openFileOutput ignores mode and builds the path by hand. It points at the same directory as getFilesDir but skips getFilesDir's mkdirs, so MODE_APPEND truncates and the first write can fail with FileNotFoundException. fileList() returns new String[0].

confirmed.title: ArgbEvaluator.getInstance() returns null, so ValueAnimator/ObjectAnimator.ofArgb and XML color animators get no evaluator
confirmed.android_behavior: getInstance() returns a shared singleton ArgbEvaluator. ofArgb() and AnimatorInflater use it (for valueType=colorType, or when values are #colors) so colors blend per channel.
confirmed.impact: ValueAnimator.ofArgb, ObjectAnimator.ofArgb (e.g. on setBackgroundColor or setTextColor) and color objectAnimators in res/animator XML interpolate the packed int, showing wrong intermediate colors. setEvaluator(null) is silently skipped. App code calling ArgbEvaluator.getInstance().evaluate(...) gets an NPE.
confirmed.suggested_fix: private static final ArgbEvaluator sInstance = new ArgbEvaluator(); return sInstance. Also needs the PropertyValuesHolder fix so the evaluator is used for int values.
confirmed.verify_reason: ArgbEvaluator.getInstance() returns null. ValueAnimator.ofArgb and ObjectAnimator.ofArgb call setEvaluator(getInstance()), and setEvaluator skips null. Direct calls to getInstance().evaluate throw an NPE. Even with a non-null evaluator, finding 0 means the int path ignores it.

confirmed.title: android:interpolator on XML <animator>/<objectAnimator> is read and then thrown away (setInterpolator block commented out)
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP loads the referenced interpolator (e.g. @android:interpolator/fast_out_slow_in, linear, overshoot) and sets it on the animator.
confirmed.impact: Every XML property animator (fragment transitions, Material state-list animators, AnimatedVectorDrawable targets, app res/animator files) runs with the default AccelerateDecelerate curve. Linear spinners ease in and out, and overshoot or bounce effects vanish. AnimationUtils.loadInterpolator(Context,int) currently returns null, so it also needs a real implementation.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Restore the block. Implement AnimationUtils.loadInterpolator(Resources, Theme, int) by parsing the interpolator XML (linearInterpolator, accelerateDecelerateInterpolator, pathInterpolator, overshootInterpolator and so on) as AOSP does.
confirmed.verify_reason: AnimatorInflater around line 1053 reads resID, then the setInterpolator block is commented out. AnimationUtils.loadInterpolator(Context,int) exists but is a stub. XML animators lose their interpolator.

confirmed.title: <propertyValuesHolder>/<keyframe> children in animator XML are parsed and discarded (loadPvh/getPVH block commented out)
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP builds one PropertyValuesHolder per <propertyValuesHolder> child, including keyframes, and sets them on the enclosing objectAnimator. Multi-property animators such as scaleX+scaleY+alpha are written this way.
confirmed.impact: objectAnimators that use <propertyValuesHolder> children (common in Material and AppCompat animator resources and AnimatedVectorDrawables) animate nothing: the values array stays null and no properties change. Combined with the PropertyValuesHolder keyframe gap, keyframe animations cannot work from XML at all.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Uncomment loadPvh, loadKeyframe, distributeKeyframes and createNewKeyframe. Add Keyframe.ofInt/ofObject and getType/getInterpolator, and keyframe support in PropertyValuesHolder.
confirmed.verify_reason: At lines 743-760 the propertyValuesHolder branch reads propertyName and valueType, the loadPvh/getPVH/values.add block is commented out, and then it only recycles.

confirmed.title: StaticLayout ignores alignment, start/end range, spacing, maxLines and ellipsize; Builder setters are all no-ops
confirmed.android_behavior: StaticLayout lays out only source[start,end), honours ALIGN_CENTER/OPPOSITE, line spacing, includePad, maxLines and ellipsizing. Builder.obtain(...).setAlignment(...).build() is the modern API.
confirmed.impact: Custom-drawn multi-line text (chart and graph labels, badges, Material chips/sliders, text-on-canvas views) is always left-aligned, never truncated with an ellipsis, may draw more lines than maxLines, and lays out the whole buffer instead of the requested range. Builder.obtain also passes align=null, so getAlignment() returns null and NPEs in code that switches on it.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Lay out source.subSequence(start,end). Pass alignment (pango_layout_set_alignment), spacing (pango_layout_set_spacing / line-height), ellipsize and height (pango_layout_set_height with negative lines for maxLines) to native. Make the Builder store its fields and construct the layout in build() with ALIGN_NORMAL as the default.
confirmed.verify_reason: The full StaticLayout constructor ignores start/end, ellipsize and maxLines; only one overload applies ellipsize. Every Builder setter returns this without storing anything, and obtain passes align=null.

confirmed.title: Character spans (ForegroundColor, BackgroundColor, RelativeSize, AbsoluteSize, Typeface, TextAppearance) discard their arguments and are never rendered
confirmed.android_behavior: Each span stores its value (getForegroundColor(), getSizeChange() and so on) and applies it via updateDrawState/updateMeasureState when TextView or StaticLayout draws the text.
confirmed.impact: Spannable-styled text is the standard way to color or bold parts of a label: search-highlight, @mentions, price strikethrough, colored status words, partial-bold. All of it renders as plain text. Apps reading span values back (getForegroundColor) fail. TextView switches to markup mode for these Spanned values without any markup, so the styling is simply lost.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Store the values and implement getters plus updateDrawState/updateMeasureState as in AOSP. In TextView/Layout, walk the spans and build a PangoAttrList (foreground, background, size scale, weight/style, underline, strikethrough, font family).
confirmed.verify_reason: ForegroundColorSpan(int dummy) {} stores nothing. Spanned text goes to native as toString() plus markup mode, so span styling is lost.

confirmed.title: TextUtils.htmlEncode returns its input unescaped; TextUtils.ellipsize never truncates
confirmed.android_behavior: htmlEncode escapes < > & ' ". ellipsize measures with the paint and returns a truncated copy with an ellipsis at START/MIDDLE/END.
confirmed.impact: Apps that build HTML for Html.fromHtml, WebView.loadData or TextView embed user text unescaped. That can break the markup (and, combined with Pango markup mode, blank the label) or inject HTML. Custom views and adapters that ellipsize titles to fit a width draw overflowing, overlapping text.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Port AOSP htmlEncode (a switch over the five characters). Implement ellipsize using Paint.measureText/breakText, or a Pango layout with ellipsize and width.
confirmed.verify_reason: TextUtils.htmlEncode returns s and TextUtils.ellipsize returns text (lines 322 and 354).

confirmed.title: MediaPlayer.setDataSource(Context, Uri) passes only uri.getPath() to a file-only GTK stream; http/content URIs and FileDescriptor sources are silently dropped
confirmed.android_behavior: MediaPlayer accepts http(s)/rtsp URLs, content:// URIs (resolved through ContentResolver), android.resource:// URIs and FileDescriptors with offset/length (how raw resources and assets are played).
confirmed.impact: Internet radio and podcast streams resolve to a bogus local path such as '/stream.mp3'. content:// files from a picker and openRawResourceFd/AssetFileDescriptor playback (common for sound effects and ringtones) produce silence with no error callback.
confirmed.suggested_fix: For http(s) use gtk_media_file_new_for_file(g_file_new_for_uri(...)). For content:// open through ContentResolver and pass an input stream or fd. For FileDescriptor+offset use a GInputStream over the fd range (gtk_media_file_new_for_input_stream). Report failures through OnErrorListener.
confirmed.verify_reason: setDataSource(Context,Uri) passes uri.getPath() to native_setDataSource(path), and setDataSource(FileDescriptor,long,long) is empty.

confirmed.title: WebView.getSettings() returns a fresh, stateless WebSettings; evaluateJavascript never calls back; user agent is the literal "GDPR VIOLATION"
confirmed.android_behavior: getSettings() returns the WebView's single WebSettings, and its setters (JavaScript, DOM storage, user agent, text zoom) take effect. evaluateJavascript runs the script and delivers the JSON result to the callback. getDefaultUserAgent returns a real Mozilla/... Chrome WebView UA.
confirmed.impact: Apps that await evaluateJavascript results (readers extracting content, OAuth or captcha helpers, hybrid apps) hang forever. Apps that use WebSettings.getDefaultUserAgent(ctx) as their HTTP User-Agent (OkHttp/Glide setups) send 'GDPR VIOLATION' to servers, which some sites block or answer with degraded pages. setUserAgentString and setJavaScriptEnabled(false) are silently ignored.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Cache one WebSettings per WebView and forward setters to webkit_settings. Implement evaluateJavascript via webkit_web_view_evaluate_javascript and deliver the result to the ValueCallback on the main thread. Return webkit_settings_get_user_agent from getDefaultUserAgent/getUserAgentString.
confirmed.verify_reason: getSettings() returns new WebSettings(), evaluateJavascript is empty, and getDefaultUserAgent and getUserAgentString return "GDPR VIOLATION". The UA value may be deliberate, but nothing in doc/ documents it, and the impact holds.

confirmed.title: Settings.Secure/Global.getString return sentinel strings ("NOTICEME", "STRING_FROM_SETTINGS_GLOBAL_WITH_KEY_...") instead of null; android_id is not hex
confirmed.android_behavior: Unknown or unset settings return null. ANDROID_ID is a 64-bit value as 16 lowercase hex digits. getInt/getFloat without a default throw SettingNotFoundException rather than returning -1/0.
confirmed.impact: Apps that check getString(...) != null and then use the value show or parse junk. For example, Settings.Global 'device_name' displays 'STRING_FROM_SETTINGS_GLOBAL_WITH_KEY_device_name', and default_input_method / enabled_accessibility_services get parsed as component names. Apps converting ANDROID_ID with Long.parseLong(id,16) or new BigInteger(id,16) crash with NumberFormatException, and every install shares one ID. try/catch(SettingNotFoundException) fallbacks never trigger and get -1/0.0 instead.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Return null for unknown keys and log once. Generate a per-install random 16-hex-digit android_id stored in the app's data dir. Throw SettingNotFoundException from the no-default getInt/getFloat variants.
confirmed.verify_reason: Settings.Secure.getString returns "NOTICEME" for unknown keys and "_totally_an_androidID" (not hex) for android_id. Global.getString returns "STRING_FROM_SETTINGS_GLOBAL_WITH_KEY_"+key. The no-default getInt and getFloat return -1 and 0.0 instead of throwing, and the code's own comments say they should throw.

confirmed.title: PreferenceManager.setDefaultValues does not write XML defaults; PreferenceActivity.addPreferencesFromResource is empty and findPreference returns a fresh ListPreference
confirmed.android_behavior: setDefaultValues inflates the preference XML and writes each android:defaultValue into the default SharedPreferences (once, tracked by _has_set_default_values). addPreferencesFromResource builds the settings list. findPreference returns the matching Preference subclass or null.
confirmed.impact: Apps that call setDefaultValues at startup and then read prefs with a different hard-coded fallback (prefs.getBoolean("notify", false) where the XML default is true) run with the wrong configuration. Legacy PreferenceActivity settings screens are blank, and casting findPreference() to CheckBoxPreference or EditTextPreference throws ClassCastException.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Implement setDefaultValues by parsing the XML (key/defaultValue for CheckBox, Switch, EditText, List and similar), writing only keys not yet present, and honouring readAgain. Make findPreference return null for unknown keys until a real preference hierarchy exists.
confirmed.verify_reason: Both PreferenceManager.setDefaultValues overloads only print STUB. PreferenceActivity.addPreferencesFromResource is empty and findPreference returns new ListPreference().

confirmed.title: AudioTrack ignores the requested encoding (always S16_LE), write(ByteBuffer) requires an array-backed buffer, getState() is hard-coded
confirmed.android_behavior: AudioTrack honours ENCODING_PCM_8BIT/PCM_16BIT/PCM_FLOAT and accepts direct ByteBuffers (ExoPlayer and most native-bridged audio use allocateDirect). getState returns STATE_UNINITIALIZED when creation fails.
confirmed.impact: Apps or players that output PCM_FLOAT or 8-bit audio play loud noise. write() with a direct ByteBuffer throws UnsupportedOperationException from array(), so ExoPlayer-based media and podcast players crash or stay silent. Init failures are reported as initialized.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Map audioFormat to SND_PCM_FORMAT_U8/S16_LE/FLOAT_LE and the frame size accordingly. For direct buffers, copy into a byte[] or add a native write taking GetDirectBufferAddress. Have native_constructor report success and make getState return 0 on failure.
confirmed.verify_reason: Native AudioTrack always uses SND_PCM_FORMAT_S16_LE (a FIXME comment is there), and the Java side assumes PCM16. write(ByteBuffer) calls audioData.array(), which throws for direct buffers. getState returns 1 with a TODO.

confirmed.title: TextView text size is applied in points, while Paint uses pixels; getTextSize() returns a fixed 10
confirmed.android_behavior: TextView.setTextSize(float) is in sp. XML textSize resolves to pixels, and getTextSize() returns that pixel size. setTextSize(unit, size) honours the unit (px/dp/sp).
confirmed.impact: TextView text renders about 1.33x larger than the same size drawn through Paint/Canvas (pt at 96 dpi vs px), so mixed custom/standard UIs look mismatched and text overflows. Code that sizes things from getTextSize() (badges, custom spans, auto-fit) always uses 10. COMPLEX_UNIT_PX/DIP sizes are treated as sp.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use pango_attr_size_new_absolute(px * PANGO_SCALE), convert units in setTextSize(int, float) with TypedValue.applyDimension, and store and return the real size from getTextSize().
confirmed.verify_reason: TextView.c setTextSize uses pango_attr_size_new (points), while Paint uses pango_font_description_set_absolute_size (pixels). TextView.java getTextSize() returns the constant 10, and setTextSize(unit,size) ignores the unit and only prints a message.

confirmed.title: TextWatcher callbacks get UTF-8 byte counts, before=0, a detached copy, and beforeTextChanged never fires
confirmed.android_behavior: In AOSP, beforeTextChanged(s,start,count,after) and onTextChanged(s,start,before,count) report the edited range in UTF-16 chars. afterTextChanged gets the EditText's own Editable, which apps edit in place (input masks, phone and credit-card formatting, max-length trimming).
confirmed.impact: count is a byte count, so non-ASCII input (accents, Cyrillic, emoji) makes s.subSequence(start, start+count) throw IndexOutOfBoundsException. before is always 0, so delete detection breaks. Formatting watchers that edit `s` have no effect, and beforeTextChanged-based logic never runs.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Track the old text and compute the changed range in UTF-16 units (or use GtkEditable insert-text/delete-text). Call beforeTextChanged, and pass an Editable that writes back to the GtkText.
confirmed.verify_reason: EditText.c changed_cb calls onTextChanged(new SpannableStringBuilder(text), 0, 0, strlen(text)), which is a UTF-8 byte count, then afterTextChanged on that detached copy. beforeTextChanged is never called anywhere.

confirmed.title: Unmapped GDK keyvals are passed through as Android keycodes; shifted symbols collide with letter keycodes
confirmed.android_behavior: In Android, KeyEvent.getKeyCode() identifies the physical key (Shift+1 gives KEYCODE_1 with META_SHIFT_ON), and unknown keys give KEYCODE_UNKNOWN. Also, repeatCount and down/event times are set.
confirmed.impact: GDK keyvals for ASCII symbols equal their ASCII codes. '!'(33) arrives as KEYCODE_E, '#'(35) as KEYCODE_G, '('/')' as KEYCODE_L/M, '*' as KEYCODE_N and '?'(63) as KEYCODE_SYM. Modifier and keypad keys (Shift_L 65505, KP_Enter, ISO_Left_Tab) arrive as out-of-range keycodes. Games, terminal emulators and apps with onKeyDown shortcuts act on the wrong keys. Times are always 0, so long-press and repeat detection breaks.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Map from the hardware keycode / unshifted keyval (gdk_display_map_keycode, or the level-0 keyval) and return KEYCODE_UNKNOWN (0) for unmapped keys. Add KP_Enter to NUMPAD_ENTER, ISO_Left_Tab to TAB, and the Shift/Ctrl/Alt keys. Fill eventTime and downTime from gdk_event_get_time.
confirmed.verify_reason: In WrapperWidget.c map_key_code, the default branch returns the raw keyval, and only a limited set of keys is mapped (exclam, numbersign, parentheses, question, Shift and KP_Enter are not). '!'=33 maps to KEYCODE_E(33), and so on. KeyEvents are built with downTime and eventTime set to 0.

confirmed.title: Matrix.setRotate(deg) adds to the existing rotation instead of resetting; preScale/preRotate with a pivot lose the pivot
confirmed.android_behavior: setRotate(deg) replaces the matrix with a pure rotation. preScale(sx,sy,px,py) and preRotate(d,px,py) apply T(-p)·op·T(p) before the existing matrix, so on identity the pivot point stays fixed.
confirmed.impact: Views that call matrix.setRotate(angle) every frame on a reused Matrix (compass needles, spinners, rotating images) spin faster and faster, because rotations accumulate. preScale/preRotate about a pivot compute S·T(-p)·M·T(p), which on identity gives a scale about the origin. Pinch-zoom and rotate gestures drift.
confirmed.suggested_fix: setRotate__JF: graphene_matrix_init_rotate(matrix, degrees, z-axis). For the pivot pre-ops, build P = T(-p)·op·T(p) as a separate matrix and then set matrix = P·matrix.
confirmed.verify_reason: setRotate__JF calls graphene_matrix_rotate_z on the existing matrix and never re-initialises it, so rotations accumulate. In preScale__JFFFF and preRotate__JFFF, graphene_matrix_translate post-multiplies, so the code builds S*T(-p)*M*T(p). On identity that reduces to S, and the pivot is lost. Compare setScale__JFFFF, which uses the correct T(-p)*S*T(p) order.

confirmed.title: SeekBar fires start, progress and stop tracking on every drag step; programmatic setProgress never notifies
confirmed.android_behavior: onStartTrackingTouch fires once at touch-down, onProgressChanged(fromUser=true) fires for each move, and onStopTrackingTouch fires once on release. setProgress() from code calls onProgressChanged(fromUser=false). change-value values are also clamped to [0,max].
confirmed.impact: Media players that seek in onStopTrackingTouch seek on every pixel of a drag (stutter, network spam). 'User is dragging' flags flip constantly, so progress updates fight the user. Labels that update in onProgressChanged stay stale after setProgress. GTK change-value can also report values outside the range.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use a GtkGestureDrag/click on the scale to emit start and stop once, clamp and round the value in change_value, and notify with fromUser=false from native_setProgress / value-changed when not user-initiated.
confirmed.verify_reason: SeekBar.c on_change_value fires start, progressChanged(fromUser=true) and stop on every change-value signal. setProgress/native_setProgress never notify the listener, and the value is cast without clamping.

confirmed.title: Path.arcTo/addArc with a 360-degree sweep draws nothing
confirmed.android_behavior: In AOSP, arcTo/addArc (and drawArc built on them) with |sweep| >= 360 draws a full oval.
confirmed.impact: With a full sweep, start and end points are equal, and an SVG arc with identical endpoints is omitted. Circular progress rings and timers disappear at 100%, and full-circle arcs in charts and gauges are missing.
confirmed.suggested_fix: If |sweep| >= 360, add a full ellipse (gsk_path_builder_add_circle or two half svg_arc_to segments). Otherwise split sweeps > 180 into two arcs.
confirmed.verify_reason: Path.c arc helper computes p2 at start+sweep. For a 360-degree sweep that equals p1 once stored as float, and an SVG arc with identical endpoints draws nothing (gsk svg_arc_to follows the SVG spec here). addArc and arcTo pass the sweep through unchanged, and Canvas.drawArc uses path.addArc.

confirmed.title: drawBitmap ignores Paint alpha (and the color filter only knows one mode)
confirmed.android_behavior: drawBitmap modulates the bitmap by paint.getAlpha(), which is used for fade-ins, disabled states and crossfades. PorterDuffColorFilter honours the given mode (MULTIPLY, SRC_ATOP, DST_IN and so on).
confirmed.impact: Bitmaps drawn with a semi-transparent Paint (image crossfades, Glide/Picasso-style fade transitions done in onDraw, dimmed icons) appear fully opaque. MULTIPLY/SCREEN tints turn into solid color silhouettes.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Wrap the texture in gtk_snapshot_push_opacity(paint->color.alpha) when alpha < 1, and build the color matrix per PorterDuff mode in native_set_color_filter.
confirmed.verify_reason: Both native_drawBitmap variants only push a color matrix and never apply paint->color.alpha. native_set_color_filter ignores the mode and always builds a constant-color matrix with alpha multiplied, which is SRC_IN behaviour, for any mode other than -1.

confirmed.title: ImageView scale types FIT_CENTER/FIT_START/FIT_END/MATRIX are ignored and CENTER scales down
confirmed.android_behavior: FIT_CENTER (the default) scales to fit, centered. FIT_START and FIT_END align to the top-left and bottom-right. CENTER does not scale and crops. MATRIX draws with getImageMatrix().
confirmed.impact: Switching an ImageView from CENTER_CROP to FIT_CENTER (common in RecyclerView rebinding and in image viewers) keeps the old COVER fit. FIT_START/END images are centered. CENTER images get shrunk. MATRIX-based zoom viewers (PhotoView and others) never move or zoom.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Map FIT_CENTER to CONTAIN explicitly. Implement FIT_START/FIT_END, CENTER and MATRIX by drawing the paintable through a snapshot transform in a custom paintable/widget rather than GtkPicture content-fit.
confirmed.verify_reason: ImageView.c setScaleType only handles FIT_XY, CENTER (SCALE_DOWN), CENTER_CROP and CENTER_INSIDE, under a TODO comment. FIT_CENTER, FIT_START, FIT_END and MATRIX fall through and keep the previous content fit. setImageMatrix is a no-op. This is a known gap marked by the TODO, not a design choice.

confirmed.title: Lifecycle: onRestart never called; onPostCreate runs before onStart
confirmed.android_behavior: Returning to a stopped activity runs onRestart → onStart → onResume. The AOSP order at creation is onCreate → onStart → onPostCreate → onResume.
confirmed.impact: Apps that refresh data in onRestart (list reloads after returning from an editor activity, re-auth checks) show stale content. Code in onPostCreate that expects onStart to have run (e.g. ActionBarDrawerToggle.syncState, state restoration helpers) sees an unstarted activity.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Track whether the activity has been stopped and call onRestart before onStart in activity_focus. Move onPostCreate after onStart in activity_start/activity_focus.
confirmed.verify_reason: Activity.c activity_start runs onCreate, then onPostCreate, then activity_update_current, which leads to activity_focus, which calls onStart. So onPostCreate runs before onStart. activity_focus never calls onRestart, and nothing else in the codebase calls onRestart().

confirmed.title: Configuration.orientation and smallestScreenWidthDp are never set; screenWidthDp uses monitor size, not window size
confirmed.android_behavior: In AOSP, orientation is PORTRAIT or LANDSCAPE, smallestScreenWidthDp = min(w,h), and screenWidthDp/screenHeightDp describe the app window. Resource qualifiers land/port/swNNNdp/wNNNdp and getConfiguration().orientation checks depend on them.
confirmed.impact: orientation stays ORIENTATION_UNDEFINED, so layout-land/-port resources and orientation checks never match. sw600dp tablet layouts are never chosen. w/h qualifiers follow the monitor (e.g. 1920 dp) rather than the 960x540 window, so apps pick large-screen layouts that do not fit the window.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Fill orientation from the window aspect ratio, set smallestScreenWidthDp = min(screenWidthDp, screenHeightDp), and base the dp values on the window size (updating on resize).
confirmed.verify_reason: Context.c monitor_changed_cb sets only screenWidthDp, screenHeightDp (from monitor geometry) and screenLayout. Nothing in the JNI code sets orientation or smallestScreenWidthDp, and Configuration defaults leave both undefined. Resources passes those values straight to AssetManager.setConfiguration.

confirmed.title: GskCanvas.drawRect drops any rectangle whose Paint has an Xfermode, including SRC_OVER and SRC
confirmed.android_behavior: drawRect blends with the Xfermode. SRC_OVER is the default behaviour, and SRC replaces the destination.
confirmed.impact: Views and libraries that always set an explicit Xfermode (e.g. new PorterDuffXfermode(Mode.SRC_OVER or SRC) for fills or highlight overlays, Canvas.drawPaint/drawColor via a paint with SRC) draw nothing, which silently blanks backgrounds and overlays. drawRoundRect, drawPath and drawCircle draw normally with the same paint, so results are inconsistent.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Treat SRC_OVER (and SRC when the paint is opaque) as a normal draw and skip only the modes that are actually unsupported, logging once. Longer term, use gtk_snapshot_push_blend or push_mask for the other modes.
confirmed.verify_reason: Confirmed: GskCanvas.drawRect returns early whenever paint.getXfermode() is not null, including SRC_OVER, while the other draw calls ignore the xfermode.

confirmed.title: VectorDrawable ignores android:fillType, so evenOdd paths are filled with the nonzero rule
confirmed.android_behavior: <path android:fillType="evenOdd"> (API 24+, emitted by Android Studio's SVG importer for many icons) fills with the even-odd rule, so inner contours become holes.
confirmed.impact: Icons converted from SVG with evenOdd (rings, donuts, letter counters like 'o' and 'e', outlined shapes) render with their holes filled in, giving solid blobs in toolbars, buttons and empty-state illustrations.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Read VectorDrawablePath_fillType (0 = nonZero, 1 = evenOdd) into VFullPath, and call path.setFillType(EVEN_ODD) on the render path before drawing that path.
confirmed.verify_reason: Confirmed: VectorDrawable.java never reads VectorDrawablePath_fillType ('fillType' does not appear in it), although the attribute exists in R.java.

confirmed.title: AccelerateDecelerateInterpolator (the default for every ValueAnimator) and PathInterpolator are linear
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP: (float)(Math.cos((input + 1) * Math.PI) / 2.0f) + 0.5f. PathInterpolator evaluates the cubic bezier or path (e.g. 0.4,0,0.2,1 for fast-out-slow-in).
confirmed.impact: Every ObjectAnimator/ValueAnimator without an explicit interpolator, and every framework PathInterpolator curve, moves linearly. Motion looks mechanical everywhere, though it does not break.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Port the AOSP formula. For PathInterpolator, port the AOSP implementation (build a lookup table from the Path or cubic control points).
confirmed.verify_reason: AccelerateDecelerateInterpolator.getInterpolation returns input. PathInterpolator ignores its arguments and returns input. ValueAnimator line 140 uses AccelerateDecelerateInterpolator as the default. Motion is only cosmetic, so the impact is low.

confirmed.title: unscheduleDrawable is a no-op, so animated drawables cannot be stopped
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP removes the posted callbacks (Choreographer/handler removeCallbacks(what, who)), so AnimationDrawable.stop(), AnimatedVectorDrawable/ProgressBar stop and setVisible(false) halt the animation.
confirmed.impact: Frame animations (AnimationDrawable loading spinners, animated icons) keep running after stop() or after the view is hidden or detached. They burn CPU, keep invalidating, and may resume visually after the app stopped them.
confirmed.suggested_fix: getHandler().removeCallbacks(runnable) for the two-argument form; for the one-argument form, removeCallbacksAndMessages(drawable) after posting with the drawable as token (postAtTime(runnable, drawable, when)).
confirmed.verify_reason: Line 1564 has a /* TODO */ body and the one-argument overload is empty, while scheduleDrawable does post via postDelayed. Posted frames cannot be removed.

confirmed.title: attachViewToParent adds a view twice when it was not previously detached
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP attachViewToParent inserts the view into mChildren exactly once.
confirmed.impact: If the view was not in detachedChildren (for example a RecyclerView view removed with removeDetachedView earlier and then re-attached, or a direct call), addViewInternal already inserts it into `children`, and the following children.add inserts it again. The child is then measured, laid out, hit-tested and iterated twice; getChildCount()/getChildAt() are off by one, which corrupts LayoutManager bookkeeping.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Return right after addViewInternal(...) in the not-detached branch, or skip children.add when the view is already in the list.
confirmed.verify_reason: When the view is not in detachedChildren and has a different parent, addViewInternal adds it to children (line 109), and attachViewToParent then calls children.add again (279). If parent == this, addViewInternal returns early and the single add is correct. The double add happens only in uncommon call orders, so impact is limited.

confirmed.title: getSuggestedMinimumWidth/Height ignore the background drawable's minimum size
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP: (mBackground == null) ? mMinHeight : max(mMinHeight, mBackground.getMinimumHeight()), and the same for width.
confirmed.impact: Custom views (and View/ImageView-like widgets using the default onMeasure) with a 9-patch or sized shape background measure to 0 or too small under wrap_content: dividers, progress tracks and badges collapse or are clipped.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Include background.getMinimumWidth()/getMinimumHeight() as AOSP does.
confirmed.verify_reason: getSuggestedMinimumWidth/Height return only getMinimumWidth/Height and ignore the background's minimum size. The default onMeasure (1448) uses them. Impact is minor.

confirmed.title: Window.peekDecorView() returns null although the decor view always exists
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP returns the decor view once it has been created, which in ATL is always (it is built in the constructor).
confirmed.impact: Code that uses peekDecorView() to find the window token or root (hide-keyboard helpers, AndroidX activity/ime helpers, dialog sizing code) takes the 'no window yet' branch and silently skips its work. The keyboard may not hide and window insets controllers are not set up.
confirmed.suggested_fix: return decorView;
confirmed.verify_reason: Window.peekDecorView returns null while getDecorView returns the decorView field that is always present.

confirmed.title: getClipToPadding()/getClipChildren() return false; AOSP defaults are true and the setters are no-ops
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP defaults both flags to true, reads them from android:clipToPadding/clipChildren, and the getters reflect the setters.
confirmed.impact: Code that branches on getClipToPadding() (LayoutManagers in custom lists, ViewPager/indicator libraries, SwipeRefreshLayout offsets) behaves as if clipToPadding=false was requested on every container, which leads to off-by-padding positioning and scroll limits.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Store both flags (default true), read the XML attrs, and return the stored values, even if clipping itself is still handled by GTK.
confirmed.verify_reason: setClipToPadding/setClipChildren are empty and both getters return false, while the AOSP default is true. Few apps branch on the getters, so impact is low.

confirmed.title: TextView.setHint is empty and getHint() returns the literal "HINT"
confirmed.android_behavior: Stores the hint and returns it. Apps and libraries (TextInputLayout, accessibility, empty-state logic) read getHint().
confirmed.impact: Code that copies or compares the hint gets "HINT", and TextInputLayout-style floating labels can show "HINT". Plain TextViews never show the hint set in XML.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Store the hint in a field, return it (null by default), and show it natively when the text is empty.
confirmed.verify_reason: TextView.setHint is empty and getHint returns "HINT". EditText overrides both correctly through the native placeholder, so only plain TextView and its non-EditText subclasses are affected, which limits the impact.

confirmed.title: ProgressBar.setIndeterminate assigns the parameter instead of the field, so isIndeterminate() never changes
confirmed.android_behavior: Updates mIndeterminate so isIndeterminate() reflects the call.
confirmed.impact: Apps and libraries that check isIndeterminate() before switching to determinate progress (download and loading UIs) make the wrong decision.
confirmed.suggested_fix: this.indeterminate = indeterminate;
confirmed.verify_reason: setIndeterminate assigns 'indeterminate = true' to the parameter, so the field never changes after the constructor. The native state is set correctly, so only isIndeterminate() is wrong.

confirmed.title: ImageButton without a src shows GTK's 'image-missing' icon
confirmed.evidence:
GtkWidget *image = gtk_picture_new_for_resource("/org/gtk/libgtk/icons/16x16/status/image-missing.png"); // show "broken image" icon
(ImageView constructor only calls native_setDrawable when a src drawable exists)
confirmed.android_behavior: An ImageButton with no src draws only its background (the icon is often supplied by a background selector, or set later from code).
confirmed.impact: Broken-image icons appear on buttons that use a background-only design, and stay there until the app sets an image. Scale type is also ignored for ImageButton (native_setScaleType is overridden as an empty method).
confirmed.suggested_fix: Create an empty GtkPicture, and apply content-fit to the inner picture so scaleType works.
confirmed.verify_reason: The ImageButton native constructor creates a picture from GTK's image-missing.png, and ImageButton.java overrides native_setScaleType with an empty body. Impact is cosmetic.

confirmed.title: Intent.addCategory ignored; getCategories always empty; getDataString returns "" instead of null
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP stores categories, so hasCategory(CATEGORY_LAUNCHER/BROWSABLE) works and categories take part in resolution. getDataString() returns null when there is no data.
confirmed.impact: Apps that branch on intent.hasCategory (e.g. launched from launcher vs deep link) take the wrong path. Apps testing getDataString()!=null treat every launch as a deep-link/open-file launch with an empty URI.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep a categories set (addCategory/removeCategory/getCategories/hasCategory) and copy it in the copy constructor. Return null from getDataString when data==null. Check that the native callers of the @Export method handle null.
confirmed.verify_reason: addCategory is a no-op and getCategories returns emptySet, so hasCategory is always false. That part holds. The getDataString-returns-"" part is weaker: the method is @Export and intent_serialize in api-impl-jni/util.c calls it to build a GVariant string, so returning null needs a native-side change. Severity lowered for that reason.

confirmed.title: Editor.putX(key, null) stores null instead of removing the key
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP commitToMemory uses `if (v == this || v == null)`, so putString(key, null) / putStringSet(key, null) removes the key.
confirmed.impact: contains(key) stays true after an app 'clears' a value with putString(key, null), and a null entry is written to the XML. Apps using contains() to detect first run or a logged-in state take the wrong branch.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Change the condition to `if (v == this || v == null)`.
confirmed.verify_reason: putString stores the null value as-is, and commitToMemory only treats v == this as a removal, so the key stays with a null value. AOSP checks v == this || v == null.

confirmed.title: Activity.moveTaskToBack and setFinishOnTouchOutside are package-private
confirmed.android_behavior: Both are public in AOSP. moveTaskToBack(true) is commonly called from onBackPressed to background the app instead of finishing it.
confirmed.impact: Calls from app code (another package) fail with IllegalAccessError at runtime, crashing apps that override back to call moveTaskToBack(true) and dialog-themed activities that call setFinishOnTouchOutside.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make both public. Keep the no-op/true semantics, or minimize the window for moveTaskToBack.
confirmed.verify_reason: moveTaskToBack and setFinishOnTouchOutside (Activity.java:701 and :705) have no access modifier, so they are package-private in android.app. App classes in other packages that call them hit IllegalAccessError at runtime.

confirmed.title: CountDownTimer delays the first onTick by one interval
confirmed.evidence:
stopTimeInFuture = SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() + millisInFuture;
handler.postDelayed(tickRunnable, countDownInterval);
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP start() sends the first message immediately, so onTick(≈millisInFuture) fires right away and then every interval.
confirmed.impact: Countdown UIs (timers, OTP resend, workout apps) show nothing or a stale value for the first interval and get one tick fewer than on Android.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use handler.post(tickRunnable) for the first tick (and account for onTick execution time like AOSP).
confirmed.verify_reason: start() calls handler.postDelayed(tickRunnable, countDownInterval) where AOSP sends the first tick immediately. The first onTick is delayed by one interval, which is minor but visible.

confirmed.title: ObjectAnimator.ofFloat(target, x, y, Path) returns an empty animator with no target
confirmed.android_behavior: AOSP approximates the Path into X and Y keyframes and animates both properties along the curve (used for arc motion and curved FAB moves).
confirmed.impact: Curved-motion animations do nothing. Because the animator has no target or values, listeners fire but the view never moves, so it ends in the wrong place when the app relies on the animation to reposition it. The same applies to the Property<> overload (line 385) and to pathData in XML (setupObjectAnimator block commented out).
confirmed.suggested_fix: Implement path keyframes: flatten the path with PathMeasure into evenly spaced points, build float keyframes for X and Y, and return ofPropertyValuesHolder(target, x, y).
confirmed.verify_reason: ofFloat(target,x,y,Path) has its body commented out and returns new ObjectAnimator() with no target or values. This is a rare API.

confirmed.title: InputFilter.LengthFilter.filter always returns "" (delete) instead of null (accept), and has no max
confirmed.android_behavior: LengthFilter keeps max and returns null (keep input) when the result fits, or the trimmed prefix otherwise. getMax() returns max.
confirmed.impact: TextView.setFilters is currently a no-op, so this is latent in widgets. However, apps and libraries that call filters manually (input validators, chat composers, AndroidX EmojiCompat and Material text field counters) treat every keystroke as rejected, and text is erased. Wiring setFilters up later will block all typing in fields with android:maxLength.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Port AOSP LengthFilter: store mMax, keep = mMax - (dest.length() - (dend - dstart)), return null/""/subSequence accordingly, and add getMax().
confirmed.verify_reason: LengthFilter.filter returns "" and ignores max. TextView.setFilters is a no-op, so this is mostly latent and only hits code that calls filters directly.

confirmed.title: android.transition: listeners are dropped (onTransitionEnd never fires) and TransitionInflater.inflateTransition returns null
confirmed.android_behavior: Listeners receive onTransitionStart/End/Cancel. Even when a transition has no visible effect, end is delivered once the scene change completes. inflateTransition returns a Transition built from res/transition XML.
confirmed.impact: Code that continues work in onTransitionEnd (Activity shared-element return, startPostponedEnterTransition chains, restoring views after TransitionManager.beginDelayedTransition) never proceeds. window.setSharedElementEnterTransition(inflater.inflateTransition(...)) passes null onward, leading to NPEs far from the cause.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Store listeners and, wherever ATL runs or skips a transition, call onTransitionStart and onTransitionEnd (posted to the main thread). Have inflateTransition parse the XML into Fade/ChangeBounds/TransitionSet, or at least return an empty TransitionSet instead of null.
confirmed.verify_reason: TransitionListener is an empty interface, addListener just returns this, and TransitionInflater.inflateTransition returns null. The impact is limited to apps that rely on onTransitionEnd.

confirmed.title: DateFormat.getDateFormat returns a date+time SimpleDateFormat; getDateFormatString is hard-coded to "dd. MM. yyyy"
confirmed.android_behavior: getDateFormat returns the locale's short date-only format (java.text.DateFormat.getDateInstance(SHORT)). getDateFormatOrder follows the locale.
confirmed.impact: Apps formatting dates with DateFormat.getDateFormat(ctx) show '11/21/26, 12:34 PM' (with time) in date-only columns such as notes, file lists and transaction lists. getDateFormatOrder always reports the Czech/Slovak day-month-year order regardless of locale, which misorders date pickers.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Return java.text.DateFormat.getDateInstance(java.text.DateFormat.SHORT) and derive getDateFormatString from that instance's toPattern() for the current locale.
confirmed.verify_reason: getDateFormat returns new SimpleDateFormat() (the locale default date+time pattern), and getDateFormatString is hard-coded to "dd. MM. yyyy".

confirmed.title: Ringtone.getTitle returns a visible placeholder string; RingtoneManager.getDefaultUri returns an empty Uri
confirmed.android_behavior: getTitle returns the ringtone's display name (or 'Default (X)' / 'Silent'). getDefaultUri returns Settings.System.DEFAULT_RINGTONE_URI, DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_URI or DEFAULT_ALARM_ALERT_URI.
confirmed.impact: Alarm, timer, reminder and messaging apps show 'FIXME: Ringtone.getTitle()' in their settings UI. The empty default Uri, stored as the chosen sound or passed to MediaPlayer or a NotificationChannel, yields silent alerts.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Return the last path segment or a 'Default' label for settings URIs. Have getDefaultUri return Settings.System.DEFAULT_RINGTONE_URI/DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_URI (and an alarm URI) by type.
confirmed.verify_reason: Ringtone.getTitle returns "FIXME: Ringtone.getTitle()" and RingtoneManager.getDefaultUri returns an empty Uri.

confirmed.title: Every view is clipped to its own bounds; clipChildren=false/clipToPadding are no-ops
confirmed.android_behavior: Clipping is controlled by the parent's clipChildren (default true) and clipToPadding. With android:clipChildren="false", children may draw outside their own and the parent's bounds. clipToPadding="false" lets list content scroll under the padding.
confirmed.impact: Overflowing badges, enlarged selected bottom-nav icons, FAB shadows and scale animations, and carousel peeking are cut off. RecyclerViews with clipToPadding=false lose their content inset.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Store clipChildren and clipToPadding on the parent, and push the clip in the parent's child snapshot only when clipChildren is true (to the padded rect when clipToPadding is true), instead of each wrapper clipping itself.
confirmed.verify_reason: wrapper_widget_snapshot always clips to its own bounds, and ViewGroup.setClipChildren and setClipToPadding are empty methods. The default (clipChildren=true clips each child to its own bounds) roughly matches Android, so only apps that rely on clipChildren=false or clipToPadding=false see a difference.

confirmed.title: getGlobalVisibleRect returns true and the unclipped rect even for views scrolled off screen
confirmed.android_behavior: getGlobalVisibleRect returns the part of the view that is visible after clipping by its ancestors, and false if none of it is visible. Lazy loaders, video autoplay, impression tracking and 'is item visible' checks use it.
confirmed.impact: Every attached view reports itself as fully visible, so autoplay starts every video in a feed, lazy loaders fetch everything, and visibility-based UI logic misfires.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Intersect the rect with each ancestor's allocation (or use gtk_widget_compute_bounds against the native window and intersect with the window size), and return false when the result is empty or the view is not drawable.
confirmed.verify_reason: native_getGlobalVisibleRect maps two corners to window coordinates and returns true. It does no intersection with ancestor or window clipping and never checks visibility. getLocalVisibleRect always returns false.

confirmed.title: text.Layout mixes UTF-8 byte indices with UTF-16 char offsets
confirmed.evidence:
jint end = (*env)->GetStringLength(env, text_jstr);
if (pango_line->length < end)
	end = pango_line->length;   /* bytes vs UTF-16 units */
...
pango_layout_index_to_line_x(pango_layout, offset, FALSE, &line, NULL); /* getLineForOffset: char offset used as byte index */
...
pango_layout_line_x_to_index(pango_line, x * PANGO_SCALE, &index, NULL); return index; /* byte index returned as char offset */
confirmed.android_behavior: All Layout offsets (getLineForOffset, getOffsetForHorizontal, getPrimaryHorizontal, line start/end) are UTF-16 char indices into the CharSequence.
confirmed.impact: For non-ASCII text (accents, Cyrillic, CJK, emoji), custom-canvas drawing draws too many characters per line, so lines overlap and duplicate. Cursor/offset math returns wrong positions (tap-to-position, link hit-testing, selection), and line start/end count code points, not UTF-16 units.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Convert between UTF-16 offsets and UTF-8 byte indices in each entry point (g_utf8_offset_to_pointer plus a surrogate-aware count), and compute end in chars from the line's byte range.
confirmed.verify_reason: In Layout.c draw_custom_canvas, end = min(UTF-16 length of the remaining text, pango_line->length in bytes). For non-ASCII lines the byte count is larger, so text from later lines is drawn too. getLineForOffset and getPrimaryHorizontal pass char offsets as byte indices, and getOffsetForHorizontal returns a byte index.

uncertain.title: isShowingLayoutBounds() returns true (debug 'Show layout bounds' mode) instead of false
uncertain.android_behavior: AOSP returns true only when the developer option 'Show layout bounds' is on; the default is false.
uncertain.impact: Any library that checks this to draw debug overlays treats ATL as being in layout-bounds debug mode. Jetpack Compose's AndroidComposeView, for example, reads layout-bounds state to decide whether to draw red/blue bounding boxes. Views can end up with debug outlines.
uncertain.verify_reason: The code returns true (added as a stub in commit 819c2330 'misc stubs for file manager apps') and AOSP defaults to false. I could not confirm that Compose or other common libraries read View.isShowingLayoutBounds() rather than the debug.layout system property, so the claimed visible impact is speculative.

uncertain.title: getFitsSystemWindows() returns true while setFitsSystemWindows is ignored
uncertain.android_behavior: AOSP default is false, it follows android:fitsSystemWindows, and setFitsSystemWindows changes it.
uncertain.impact: AndroidX code that branches on ViewCompat.getFitsSystemWindows (CoordinatorLayout, AppBarLayout, CollapsingToolbarLayout, DrawerLayout, BottomSheetDialog) treats every view as insets-consuming, which leads to wrong status-bar scrim and padding decisions and offsets in drawers and app bars.
uncertain.suggested_fix: Store the flag, default false, read View_fitsSystemWindows in the constructor, and return the stored value.
uncertain.verify_reason: getFitsSystemWindows returns true and the setter is empty, so the code is wrong. But ATL reports empty WindowInsets, so the branches the finding names probably consume nothing. The real impact is unclear.

uncertain.title: Spanned text switches the GtkLabel into markup mode but passes the plain toString(), so '&' or '<' breaks the label and the spans are dropped
uncertain.android_behavior: Android renders the Spanned with its spans. The string content is shown literally, whatever characters it contains.
uncertain.impact: Html.fromHtml("Terms & Conditions") (toString gives "Terms & Conditions") or any SpannableString containing '&' or '<' is re-parsed as Pango markup. The parse fails, so the label shows an empty or wrong string and GTK logs warnings. Bold, colour and link spans are never shown. This is common for about screens, formatted strings and HTML-from-resources.
uncertain.suggested_fix: Either convert spans to escaped Pango markup (g_markup_escape_text on the text runs plus span tags) or keep use_markup off and convert spans to a PangoAttrList. Never enable markup on unescaped plain text.
uncertain.verify_reason: The code matches the description, but the example is wrong. ATL's Html.fromHtml deliberately returns a SpannableString that keeps the raw HTML source (minus br/nbsp), and the label renders it as Pango markup, so '&' stays valid. This is the intended way fromHtml works. The breakage is real only for other Spanned text containing a raw '&' or '<' (for example SpannableString, or TextView.append, which produces a SpannableStringBuilder). Real spans are dropped either way.
